s: Kryptos: A Picture and a Million Words
t:
Cleopatra VII Thea Philopator 69 BC - 30 BC, 42 BC Cleopatra and Antony

In the research I’ve done, I’ve been looking for a person, place or something unifying that would tie together four key ideas and civilizations and well as a number of other items I consider clues found throughout the Kryptos sculpture and courtyard exhibit. That appears to be the case in the relationship between Cleopatra, Mark Antony and their family.Cleopatra was a Macedonian Greek queen of the Ptolomeic Dynasty and one of the last pharaohs of Egypt, consort to the Roman Mark Antony, mother of her first-born son Caesarion by Julius Caesar and the twins Alexander Helios and Cleopatra Selene. Least notable of these is the incestuous marriage to her brother Ptolemy. On the pages of history, you might call it palimp-cest.

As part of the Ptolemeic line and by her own doing, Cleopatra was already steeped in the divine, considered a mortal manifestation of a goddess as  Isis-Aphrodite juust one of many incarnations of the same goddess such as Aphrodite-Urania. Caesar had pretensions towards divinity before his death, and Antony was openly referred to as the New Dionysus. Caesarion was considered the divine child of Isis – Horus, entailing all that goes with the Eye of Ra and Eye of Horus. He was further titled as the "King of Kings," a threatening title that would later also be assigned to Jesus Christ 30 years after Caesarion’s death. Alexander Helios was named for the sun god Helios, his sister Cleopatra Selene for the moon goddess.

Alone, Cleopatra’s life is a huge body of work, and narrowing it down in a meaningful fashion requires uniting key concepts to highlight a point or place in time. I theorize that to be the time and place highlighted in the painting The Triumph of Cleopatra wherein Cleopatra, clad in flowing robes and at rest upon her throne rides one of her purple winged ships encompassed in a shroud of perfumed mist, its movement propelled by a row of neatly matched rays in the form of oars as adoring throngs look on from around peripteral columns notable in the temple of deified Caesar, Divus Iulius.

This painting of Cleopatra is a cut-away of one of the last pharaohs in voyage from Alexandria by way of the world wonder Pharos Lighthouse (ancient even in her time), past Cyprus/Kypriss (Aphrodite) of the Hidden Affairs, to the city of Tarsus. Laden with extravagant gifts for her first meeting with Marc Antony, it was a  first meeting between tragically doomed lovers.

In noting Pharos on her voyage, it’s worth pointing out a few special features of that lighthouse: a powerful furnace, not unlike the heat in a hot air balloon to feed smoke signals by day, and a great ray of light by night. This ray was the product of a large bronze mirror designed to reflect the flame’s light..

In return for her gifts, she would receive two particularly notable ones here: the Cilician territory that included Tarsus and the island of Cyprus. You could say he "abs"cised (cut way) them from the Roman Empire to her in return for her loyalty.

When looking at this voyage from a bird’s eye view, there a two most notable things – one, the path between Alexandria and Tarsus is an angle very similar to that in the coordinates (and to 0631425), and secondly, if one were to take the hints in that old coded message as a clue, depending on where one looked at the beginning of the journey or the return home, one could state:

T(arsus) IS YOUR POSITION. NO, IT IS O(ld) P(haros).

Conclusion? This theoretical concept suggests a couple specialized possibilities, two immediately coming to mind though one is less likely than the other.

3d Tetrahedron (4 sides, */3/5/7/9 rows no apex on the pyramid, no apex on the pyramid, adding up to 48/48/48/49.

Masked Scytale (seems to require a physical object or something that would suggest one)

~ James

The shorter path ...

1.

38.9522° N, 77.1457° W

~ Kryptos coordinates

"CTF SEVENTY-SEVEN X WHERE IS RPT WHERE IS TASK FORCE THIRTY FOUR RR THE WORLD WONDERS."

~ Communication between Task Force 38 and Task Force 77.

There are some interesting parallels in this bit of history of the Battle of Leyte Gulf with the Morse Stones that I won’t go into here.

2.

This leads to..

We all know the bit in K2 regarding "only WW knows the exact location" and that Jim identified this as William Webster.

 However, there’s a matching concept in K3 – SLLSLLNOHSNOS

If you treat the S and L as short and long in morse, that’s WW NOHS NOS. The second string doesn’t make much sense unless you are familiar with phonemic pronunciation – NOHS = KNOWS if you say it aloud. So there’s a second string with a shadow callback to the first, and as noted in that excerpt, there’s padded text referring to World Wonders. Meaningless in context, something else entirely here. We don’t have any assertion from Jim that it necessarily means William Wesbster and it strikes as a notable clue to something else. Supposed we read it as (W)orld (W)onders – Knows/Nose/Nos. Phonemic is open to a lot of interpretation, but the apparent link to the plaintext of K3 is not – "Wondrous Things" are the first things Howard Carter sees in the ray of his light.

3.

 There are 7 of those Wonders, one being the Pyramid of Giza with its associated broken-nosed sphinx, but there’s one I’m more interested in. That’s the Pharos Lighthouse at Alexandria, for a lot of reasons I’ve gone over in other previous posts, but most importantly for the example of the Pharaoh Tut, as well as the other Pharaohs responsible for Pharos and Giza. There’s a line of connected association.

4.

Pharos and Pharaohs, with their phonemic similarity, and the KNOWS/NOS/NOSE concept kicked another association:
ID BY(FAR?) ROWS VS X LAYER TWO.

Imagine both as instruction and consider the ciphertext to be Layer One. Layer two would be the plaintext. ID by Rows suggests ordered rows, which does not exist in Kryptos, but DOES exist in the Kryptos Prototype at Jim’s home. That’s a project that I’ve done, rows of 24 in exclusively plaintext, that yielded results.

"Far Rows" describes the left and right columns (turn sideways to make them ordered rows) They are notable as they create a series of null ciphers in K2/K3 left and K1-K3 left-right that I’ve also described elsewhere. This is a "Wondrous Things" pattern, similar circuitous text  on a cup found first in Tut’s tomb, the Lotus Chalice. So, you now have

PHARAOHS/PHAROS/FAR ROWS

5. The modified grid carries this as well. INSIDE K1 at the beginning of each word of plaintext, is the null cipher T IS AST BALLON, reaching between the two FAR ROWS like an unpatterned sky of stars, setting a visualized backdrop to a hot air balloon floating across the sky.

I
’ve come across variations incarnations of the "doomed lovers" story in associations with my research, a concept that is referred to as "star-crossed lovers", something Cleopatra and Antony are famous for being.

Conclusion:  This may be the short way around my body of research and there is more to this "original matrix" in terms of visual effect than immediately meets the eye.

s: On the topic of botched encryptions
t:
I understand Bill's call for a double-check on encryption. Afterall, once a cipher reaches some age, botched encryption is a favorite out. As I've said in the past, I've dealt with a bunch of one-time home brewed systems as part of another contest, and the things they've all had in common are:

1. They are unsolvable until you have enough information about the encryption mechanism to match the level of detail used to design the system by the creator.

2. They almost always have spelling errors.

3. They are almost always appear unsolvable until you've you're privvy to #1

4. Some dynamic rule is what keeps #1 and #3 true.

Take the D'Agapeyeff Cipher. Jim Gillogly suggested it was a botched encryption after his failure to decrypt it. It's more likely due to it being a one-off system that would-be solvers just didn't free their mind enough and use the clue available to solve it.

I believe Kryptos K4 belongs in the same pile.

Food for thought:  If the Cyrillic Projector used anything other than phonetic substitution and misspellings for it's masking technique, it too would remain unsolved right now with no further clues about how it was masked.

Plain -> Masked Plain (phonetic spellings which didn't alter the IC enough to keep it hidden) -> Vigenere encrypted with keyword in plain sight (MEDUSA) set off by a different font -> Ciphertext.

If K4 were to be:  Plain -> Masked Plain via an unspecified algorithm -> Vigenere encrypted with HYDRA -> Ciphertext

Then we'd literally have the same process as the Cyrillic Projector with a higher degree of difficulty due to the masking algorithm compressing the IC from 6.8+ to ~3.6 rather than what you saw with the Cyrillic Projector taking the normal IC from ~5.5 to something just slightly lower but still detectable via frequency counting.

s: Kryptos Parallels: WWII Battle of Leyte Gulf and Crossing the T
t:
A little less Greek, and a little mores Morse...

In the previous post I noted the striking similarity not just between the World Wonders cryptogram with my own research, but the Task Force numbers (38 and 77) corresponding with the Kryptos coordinates.  There is of course the SOS for the missing Task Force 34 as well. A little further reading on the Battle of Leyte brings up some other interesting potentially related stuff…

The quote itself, as relates to the battle, ended in a misunderstanding due to the receiving unit forgetting to remove the Padding text (The World Wonders) and that omission being taken as criticism. A failure to maintain a lucid memory of proper procedure, you could say.

The Battle of Leyte is notable for the use of a tactic referred to as "Crossing the T" a classic naval maneuver that allows one fleet to bring raking fire to bear (limitations of their guns at the time) on another fleet crossing in front of them. The T position is the point of attack or ambush. The Task Force specifically responsible for this maneuver was Task Force 77.

The battle was in response to a series of raids by Task Force 38 on the RYukyu Islands as well as some pre-battle attacks by submarines Dace  and Darter, ambushing the Japanese Center Force. Task Force 38 was shadowed by Japanese aerial reconnaissance, but their Third Fleet formation apparently was virtually invisible to them, and went undetected. The concept of all these islands are interesting in that they seem reminiscent of Langley's islands of Morse stone in the grass, as well as those in the courtyard.

~ James

I like your 2.  But I like it as a supplement to my own pet theory (pardon my cultural appropriation) that WW alludes to Woodrow Wilson (him as wouldn't stoop to reading someone else's mail), which is a further allusion to the Wilson Primes, i.e., five, thirteen and five hundred sixty-three.  I was astonished & delighted at the time I found 563 hinted at, and have since been wondering whether the 5 and the 13 were to be used as well.  Assuming you were onto something with "WW  NOHS NOS", that would seem to hint that they are.  Also, of course, assuming that 563 is regarded as one number, and that WW only 'nohs' 5, 13 & 563, and is not concerned with such nos. as might thereafter be derived from them in further steps.

-Carl Ellis.

s: On the topic of botched encryptions
t:
Second that.  I have never been able to believe that there is a character carved on those copper plates that was not intended to be carved where it was carved.  We're told Ed spent months of evenings playing with this.  We have an idea of the time involved in actually creating this, and the money that went into it.  I'm sure Ed & Jim were able to imagine what the reaction would be like if they managed to botch it, and I don't see them fancying their work becoming the famous Irremediably Botched Tower of Cryptography.  Not that there can't be "errors" &/or misspellings that will not hurt the cryptography - one of my own wilder guesses expects one at K4/23; but I say this thing will not turn out to have been fatally flawed.  I don't mind asking them to check the work and report if they're willing, but I'd bet heavily they nailed it - it's we that haven't.

Carl Ellis

s: Kryptos: Padding and Patterns - EMU to UME
t:
This one's going to be short and to the point:

    In previous posts about the WWII Battle of Leyte Gulf, I've repeatedly reference the semifamous Turkey Trots/World Wonders cipher, and one of the parts that has interested me in terms of Kryptos is the concept of "padding" that these phrases in the message represent. I wondered if Jim might have applied some sort of personal take on that.

   While examining a model Kryptos someone submitted to the photo stream, I noticed something: the EMU and reflected UME. EMU is the obvious first three letters of K1, and UME is a reflected pattern that shows up on the last row of K2. I wondered if that meant something, and noticed that there's 26 letters after UME.

   Taking that a step further, on rows 3 and 6 there's a pairing of "EE". Depending on how one cares to interpret the space between them, that's a separation of 96 to 98 letters.

Conclusions: Embedded alphabet, some sort of take on OTP?

James N.

s: Kryptos: Wondrous Patterns - EMU/UME, WET/DRY and Lies
t:
I've been hung up on DESPARATLY for awhile because I believe in consistency of clues, and it hasn't been until some things clicked in place with these recently noticed patterns and the concept of phonemics in WW NOSE/KNOWS/NOS/NOHS. These are two strings of text from K1/K2 and K3.

DESPARATLY = DES PAR AT LY = DES/(W)RAP AT LIE

YRDMFDVFPJUDEEHZWET

DEEHZ ct  = TOTAL pt

Note: ends in total-ly

The lie – it’s virtually invisible, not totally.

TEWPIEROAGRIEWFEB AECTDDHILCEIHSITEGOEAOSDDRY

"OM THE CHAMBER CAUSED THE FLAME TO FLICKER BUT PRESEN"

DD,DD ct  =FL, ES pt (SELF)

Note: ends in present-ly

The lie – The flickering effect is not the flame but the self’s perception of the flame. An illusion.

Observations:

The obviously reversing WET/DRY dynamic. Two points:

Correlation to shining rays of light through dry ice, i.e. Jim’s HYDRA 2009 exhibit

"Wondrous things" – The Lotus Chalice uses this dynamic in its writing of two inscriptions circling back to back.

EMU = electro magnetic units? D = electric field displacement unit of measure?

This appears to be a reference to submarines and diffuse lighting camouflage in WWII particularly as relates to the Battle of Leyte.

Periscope = eye?

Conclusions:

Wrapped alphabet using only 26 letters? Something like:
 MLKJIHGFEDCBA []ZWYXVUTSRQPON

and other possible combinations with a split alphabet.

The null is intentional.

~ James N

Notes from Day 1 at Langley

Security is tight tight tight. Multiple layers of review to enter, then driving through multiple gates.

Exciting to walk through the Main Entrance across the CIA compass rose, I didn't get to do that last time.

Sobering to see the Memorial Walls.

Escorted in by multiple people, and had some interesting chats with members of the Media Relations and Public Affairs departments, they were eager to talk about Kryptos. We spoke briefly about "the envelope" and where it might be now. CIA lore is that it was in the Director's office. Though I've also heard that Webster gave it to Peter Earnest, who later became the founding executive director of the International Spy Museum. I heard today that Mr. Earnest was in the process of retiring, or at least stepping down from that Board.

I spent nearly an hour in the gift shop, spending waaaay too much money, but then again, I'm not regretting a penny of it!

On our tour of the building we passed a row of portraits of CIA directors, including William Webster. On my brief glance as we walked by I didn't notice anything unusual, though I would like to go back and take a closer look.

The museum was interesting, I could spend much more time there! They had silken OTPs, a make-up box with an encrypted mirror, and lots of other intriguing items.

The high point of the day for me was as we were walking past the cafeteria, and I knew I was getting closer to seeing Kryptos again!

We came in from the far end of the courtyard on this cold cold day. The first thing I noticed was that there's a new concrete plaza in the semi-circle that Sanborn designed.  The plaza doesn't go as far as the duck pond, nothing of that part of the sculpture was disturbed. There were two walkways leading to the new plaza, one from the far side, and another perpendicular, that led from near the K2 coordinates point.

Near the coords I saw a roughly benchmark-sized disk. No markings, but a large slot in it like for turning. On further investigation, there were several of these disks placed each 15' or so around the circumference of the grassy area. I'm not sure what they're for.

Approaching the duck pond area, I was excited to see that the pond is drained for the winter. I looked closely but saw nothing inside of interest, just the normal pump/filtration items. There were some extra rocks here and there which seemed to be placed to hide the pump lines. If I looked at it with the eyes of a geocacher, I spotted several potential (but unlikely) hiding spots for a cache, we'll see if I can examine more closely tomorrow.

Approaching Kryptos, the first thing I noticed was that the white rock is no longer white, it is now a distinct tinge of green.

The round pool, as with the duck pond, is also drained. I saw nothing of interest inside.

All of the letters on Kryptos seemed to be in their correct locations.  :)

The weather was overcast, so there was nothing light- or shadow-related to be observed.

I didn't get a chance to go outside the New Headquarters Building to see the Morse pieces or whether the unmarked slab is still visible. That will be tomorrow!

The biggest disappointment of the day was hearing that I won't be able to bring in a GPS tomorrow, so I will have to get creative to identify the exact location of the K2 coordinates.  From eyeballing it on Google Maps, it looks like I can triangulate from two known points. For example, from Kryptos (the petrified log), on my first measure I get a distance of 177.6'.  From the edge of the new walkway, I get 41.87'.  If anyone has different numbers, or knows a better way to triangulate this, please let me know ASAP, as I will have to leave my phone in the car so will not have access to email after 0845.

I will head back for Day 2 tomorrow, plans are for the crew to interview Ed Scheidt, and then getting some footage of me walking around and exploring/measuring the various pieces.  Then we go to a different location for another interview in the afternoon.  The next day, Sunday, we all meet at Sanborn's studio for more Kryptos conversation.

Will post more as I know it!

Elonka  :)

Day 2 at Langley

I took another look around the K2 coords location, but again, saw nothing unusual. I also had the opportunity to more closely examine the sandstone benches, and even got down on the ground and examined them from underneath, but saw nothing unusual.

Along with seeing Kryptos (similar observations to yesterday), I went out to see the NHB Front Entrance pieces. My first reaction was how much bigger the compass rose was from what I'd expected. For some reason I'd pictured it as being a foot in diameter. Instead it was more like 2+ feet in diameter.

I was also surprised at the size of the "unmarked slab", and that it was three-dimensional, not just one slab set into the grass, but at a slant as the other pieces were. It was about 5' in length, and about 20' away from the other pieces. It had no other unusual markings that I could see.

There were no other slabs than the three sections we know about. I was especially looking carefully in the flower gardens (since it was winter and therefore easy to look through them). I saw nothing noteworthy, no extra lodestone, no rocks of any kind.

Up close, the unmarked piece looked even more like an arrow. I followed the line as far as I could, but saw nothing Kryptos-related. The line goes past a K-9 area, a place for washing dogs. There's also a tree there with a memorial plaque, that has neither a name nor a date (will post details on it later). It wasn't tarnished, so didn't look like something that had been there for 30 years. The tree was also fairly young.

I spent quite a bit of time looking for anything that looked like a copper disk or a USGS marker. I looked up and down the walkway, then up against the building, on both sides of the walkway. I went as far as I could in both directions, but eventually there is a steep hill on either side.

I confirmed that the lodestone was indeed magnetic by holding my visitor badge up to it. The lodestone was large, maybe bowling-ball size. I examined closely to see if there was there was any additional morse underneath it but did not see anything.

Took lots of pics, over 1,000, in prep for a 3D model. I hope it's enough! Once I have time to catch my breath, I'll figure out a good way to share them.

Will post more later!

Elonka  :)

Elonka Dunin
Drew Beebe (producer)
Jon O'Beirne (producer / cameraman)
Andy Lampard (cinematographer / cameraman)
Dennis "Denny" McDaniels, retired NSA (from 1992 team)
Bob Mang
Carl Ellis
Richard Santa Coloma
Mike Godwin

Jim's studio was full of all sorts of goodies. Various shapes and sizes of Kryptos miniatures, plus samples of artwork from all other parts of his career: Atomic Time, Covert Obsolescence, projected light photographs, and his newest work about the black market sculpture trade in Cambodia.

We plied everyone with sushi and munchies and chatted for hours while the crew filmed away, then they kicked most of out so they could do about 45 minutes just with Jim, then they spent more time getting various shots, such as one of the cameramen went outside to get a shot through the windows of Jim looking at some of his crypto (Cyrillic) matrices.

We did a lot of Kryptos Q&A, here are the high points:

* When asked about the out-of-alignment letters and whether they had anything to do with K4, Jim kind of glanced at Ed and asked/considered whether it was time, and then told us that no, those letters were intended to refer to "1-2-3". That they'd been commonly perceived as misaligned, but their intent was actually much more subtle than that.

* When asked whether it was necessary to know the solutions to 1-3 in order to solve 4, Jim said no.

* Jim referred often to the fact that he had done the encryption on his drive back across the country, that it hadn't been fun. While he was talking, I noticed his body language, he would glance down next to him as though remembering seeing the text on the seat next to him. He said that for 1-3 he had used matrices which had to be turned, like "right-right". He didn't quite say that he'd used matrices for K4, but used verbs such as turn and flip, and that he had put it "through the washing machine".

* We asked him if he'd be willing to go off with Ed and just run through K4 as a test, and he said no. When I asked him if he would be able to describe K4's method to Ed, Jim said he didn't know.

* Jim said he's going to offer another clue in 2019, "a year ahead of schedule" and that this would be "the last one".

* When asked about his favorite Berlin clock, he said he likes "both Berlin clocks". He emphasized the word "both".

* When asked about the solutions that have been sent to him, and whether any of them were close, Jim said he got one from Germany about a year ago that was "kind of scary", that the first part had started to look right, but then the rest didn't.

Other notes:

Jim made it clear that encrypting Kryptos was something he did decades ago, and he's done his best to actively forget it. Forget the plaintext, forget the methods.

He also made it clear that he didn't like math, it was "anathema", he called himself something like a "math-anathema", but I don't remember exactly.

When he's told that Kryptos is in people's Algebra textbooks, he finds it funny. Especially when it's near the algorithm sections. That he absolutely is not a cryptanalyst. When people write to him and ask him this question or that question about different techniques, he's just lost. He knew how to make a code, but not how to take them apart, so it's never any good for us to ask him those kinds of questions.

Some of Jim's answers were not consistent with things he's said in the past. For example, in one of my first conversations with him many years ago I asked him about the Q in "iqlusion", and he said that it was deliberate, but it's not what it was that was important, it was the orientation or positioning. Today though he said that it was probably an error, that when he compared his two matrices, he saw a Q on one but not on the other. He also admitted the error in K2. But he did refer today to other "deliberate" errors. The topic clearly made him uncomfortable, like he was embarrassed to make a mistake, and he even started to get rattled and confused about whether "ID by Rows" or "Layer Two" was the correct plaintext, so I didn't want to push it too hard.

When asked whether it's necessary to know anything about the Kryptos surroundings to solve K4, Jim said that surroundings would of course change, so it would have been kind of dumb (silly?) to do that.

If he does have someone send him the correct answer, his first call will be to John Schwartz at the New York Times.

It's not necessary to have a particular book to solve K4, just "to be able to read".

Around the time that he was creating Kryptos, Jim was reading a Tom Robbins novel, "Still Life with Woodpecker", one of Jim's favorites. (note from Elonka: isn't there a hidden message on a pack of Camels in the book, which comes out to "CHOICE"?  Which of course may or may not be related to K4)

The front entrance pieces with the Morse code messages were meant, artistically, to represent that stone strata with messages had been there before the CIA, and we were seeing them as stone outcroppings. And that as we got deeper and deeper into CIA, the messages were intended to become more and more complex.

When asked about Star Trek (TNG started in the late 1980s), Jim said he has watched the show, but he doesn't remember episode names so couldn't say what his favorite was.

We spent quite a bit of time asking Jim about the correlation between the plaintext BERLIN and the ciphertext such as NYPVTT. Specifically, we were trying to find out if there was a 1:1 relationship from NYPVTT to BERLIN, or there was some other step, the masking technique. Jim was confused when we mentioned masking technique, evidently it's something that Ed said that Jim didn't understand. Jim said that yes the ciphertext and plaintext were connected, but when I tried to explain what exactly we were asking, like that in K1 EMUFPH is exactly BETWEE, but in K3 ENDYAH does not map exactly to SLOWLY, Jim backed off and said he would only commit to the fact that K4 is exactly 97 characters long, and that BERLIN is plaintext that starts at exactly the 64th character, but he wouldn't go further than that.

Jim spoke a bit about the people who are writing to him via jimsanborn.net, with $50 and a request for correspondence. He says he gets one person writing to him every week, at the same time, with a potential solution, that it's basically the same but shifts one letter each time!

Some other bits and pieces I learned about Ed Scheidt, from his 30-odd years in the CIA.

In his early years he was stationed in Laos, "seeing the countryside" meaning that he was out in the fields as a communications officer.

He was in Syria during the war in 1967, and was the last one out, the one who "closed the vault".

He was also in the Philippines. Sadly, that was where his first wife died, in Manila in childbirth.

He was never in Cambodia.

Ed's 2nd (current) wife, Mary-Jane, was executive assistant to CIA Directors such as George Tenet (who was Director from 1996-2004). Next time I see her, I'll have to ask if she ever saw anything Kryptos-related in the office!

As for the documentary crew, they've got hours of footage now. From this point they'll edit it down to a short piece, probably about five minutes long, which will eventually be available at greatbigstory.com. I'll be staying in touch with them, and will of course let you know if/when I get transcripts of the interviews, and additional Kryptos pictures/videos.

And now, I sleep!

Elonka  :)
One correction, it wasn’t Bob Mang, it was Bob Bogart, sorry!

My takeaways:

1. Sanborn was intentionally misleading for a long time.
2. He’s created a one-off system with likely no regard for how difficult he made it.
3. K4 is certainly unsolvable based on his description.

He should be ashamed for being so smug rather than being repeatedly lauded for being some kind of genius. It’s easy to make something unsolvable, and any crackpot can do that. It’s a whole-nother thing to be able to understand the implications of what you’ve done and allow just enough clues or leaps of faith to leave a solution path.

I’m glad to have this closure.

Nice job on pressing him on everything, Elonka & Co.

Jim

(...)  If Jim just put it out on a plate for someone to solve based on his hints to date then he'd compromise the integrity of the piece.  If the wording, puzzles and clues we're supposed to solve are equally as cryptic then wouldn't we expect Jim to speak to this same language?  Maybe that has led to a perception of him speaking with forked tongue over the years, but personally I love it!!!
I'd like to think that the clues he's given to date are carefully chosen to aid verification when someone is on the right path, but not explicit enough to allow any backwards engineering.

One of the original objectives for the piece was that it should engender feelings of well being and hope.  What better way to do that than take the agency staff and then the whole world on a big adventure!

The CIA by its very nature objectifies foreign individuals and scans them for threat, always alert to the potential threat of outsiders, but this piece redresses that balance and invites the world back in by uniting people in a common quest.  That is something political leaders have consistently failed to do, so by that measure alone Jim is indeed a genius!!!

Kind regards,
Matt

s: Kryptos: Wondrous Patterns II: YRD/WET, TEW/DRY, and the Eye in the Sky
t:
The basics, following this path laid out in the previous post:

FEET WET and FEET DRY are old Morse aircraft  prosigns..

Feet Wet = Contact is over water

Feet Dry = Contact is over land

WET/DRY POLICY also carried the added expectation that Feet Wet contacts would be conducted in cipher

K1. Affected text "ION (eye on) it was total"

K3: Affected text "Flame to flicker"

If we consider how that applies to the affected cipher text, it would suggest that the illusion of invisibility is noted while over water, and the flickering flame while over land would be the reflection of light on the periscope’s eye, while from above, diffusing lighting camouflage would make the periscope, (not to mention the entire submarine) nearly invisible.

Why specifically the periscope? Other than the previous discussion of the WWII Battle of Leyte in the Phillipine islands It has a great deal in common with the Pharos lighthouse – that is the reflection of light back and forth with a mirror. Where Pharos used a single mirror, the periscope uses several. All in light rays, of course. This metaphor between Pharos ad a periscope  is neither original nor mine.

The reversing effect is, of course, the most important piece of that periscopic "eye", as it runs parallel to the reversing TEW/DRY text in the Kryptos sculpture.

Conclusion? This may reflect the use of an alphabet with multiple reversals.

~ James

s: Kryptos: Wondrous Patterns III - Reflection, Throne & Kylix
t:
Retreading some previous ground to refresh my memory, and things now seem to be circling back to it in more interesting ways.

I’ve referred repeatedly to the Lotus Chalice, alternatively known as the King’s Wishing Cup and the alabaster chalice. This item is notable, as it presented as one of the first "wondrous things" that Howard Carter laid eyes on when looking into Tut’s tomb. This is an ancient drinking cup featuring a series of glyphs encircling the rim – two phrases that reflect outward from each meant to be read right to left and left to right, much like: I LOVE KRYPTOS [] NROBNAS MIJ or perhaps TEW/DRY and YRD/WET

These inscriptions are preceded by the image of Horus falcon and the ankh. Also notable, the chalice has the king’s THRONE name (as opposed to the Horus and Nebty names)

The item itself, the chalice, is known as a KYLIX, a drinking cup.

This also circles back to the null ciphers. The introduction of the submarine puts T IS AST BALLOON and T IS FLOWING ROBES in intriguing different lights of metaphor, but the T IS HROHNL goes straight to the Lotus Chalice.

HROHNL is notable as the series of ciphertext directly connected to DYAHR, most interesting as a potential puzzle because of it’s phonemic and morse possibilities.

We’ve used the WW morse SLL SLL in K3 to note the NOS/NOHS/NOSE phenomenon. If we consider the "L" as morse, it changes to HROHN(T). If T IS YOUR POSITION, the T should begin at the left = THROHN = phonemic THRONE.

The name of whomever sits on the THRONE is a deeper mystery and not really relevant, I don’t think, but valuable for pointing attention back to the Kylix, and that convention of mirrors and reflections.

Reflecting Pool.

Reflected Vigenere

TEW/DRY

YRD/WET

Reflection text inscriptions.

Periscope mirrors, Pharos mirrors, reflected rays.

Conclusion: Conceptually, it boils down to reflecting text. KYLIX as a possible keyword?

~ James

s: 2013 Kryptos Dinner: Notes from Richard SantaColoma
t:
In seeing Richard at the recent event, he reminded me that he had
    sent me his notes about the 2013 dinner, but I hadn't sent them to
    the Group. So, here you go!

    ******************************************************************

    Kryptos Notes

    I was invited to a dinner discussing the
      Kryptos sculpture,
      and the problems of the unsolved panel 4 of the sculpture, since I
      was
      attending the NSA Crytological Conference in October of 2013. The
      dinner was
      arranged by Elonka Dunin for Saturday, October 19. I wanted to
      write these
      notes down so that I would remember certain details from that
      night.

    Attending were Elonka, of course, Klaus Schmeh
      and David
      Suter, all three of which I know from my Voynich Manuscript
      studies. The talk after
      dinner was given by Edward Scheidt, the designer of the ciphers
      used in
      Kryptos. Elonka gave the accompanying slide presentation, which
      included
      various documents she retrieved via the Freedom of Information
      act, from the
      NSA, relating to their attempts at decoding the panels of Kryptos.

    Also present was Jim Sanborn, the artist who
      designed
      Kryptos; one or two of the NSA cryptographers who solved panels 1
      through 3,
      and various other figures in the world of cryptography, amateur
      and
      professional, whom I do not know. About 30 to 40 people were
      present.

    Notes:

    - In light of the fact that Sanborn had, in
      November of
      2010, given the clue that “letters 64-69 NYPVTT in part 4 encode
      the text
      BERLIN”, several questions were asked about this. One question
      was, “Then you
      are saying that N=B, Y=E, etc.?”. Sanborn answered to the
      positive, while Ed
      seemed less ready to acknowledge this. I do not know if this is
      because of a
      misunderstanding of the question, or because of Ed’s reluctance to
      go that far,
      or because Ed himself was not entirely certain if this was the
      final outcome.
      However, as Ed professes to not know the actual answer, although
      he knows the
      cipher type used, he therefore should know whether or not there is
      an actual
      letter for letter correspondence. So I came away from the answer
      thinking that
      either Sanborn did not exactly know what was being asked, or that
      there is this
      letter for letter correspondence. I favor the latter.

    - Ed Schiedt made the point that (paraphrasing
      as close as I
      can remember), “Panel four’s cipher was designed so that English
      could not be
      used as an aid in deciphering”. Questions were asked about this
      statement,
      among them, “Are you saying it is not in English?”, and Ed seemed
      reluctant to
      answer directly… only repeating “…English could not be used as an
      aid”. So my
      take on that is that it is either not in English, or the system
      employed would
      obviate any attempts  at
      using character
      counts to solve it.

    - As for the “BERLIN” clue, it occurred to me
      on the way
      home that the inclusion of this word may have something to do with
      the fall of
      the Berlin Wall. When I got home I checked the date the wall
      “fell”, and
      officially that would be November 9, 1989. The Kryptos sculpture
      was officially
      dedicated November 3rd, 1990… almost exactly a year
      later.
      Considering the importance of the “fall of the wall” at this time,
      and also
      considering the “wall-like” nature of the Kryptos work, and also
      considering
      the importance in espionage in the Cold War, I do consider it a
      good
      possibility that panel 4 of the Kryptos deals with this issue. I
      also wonder if
      Sanborn felt compelled to reveal “BERLIN”, as we are so far out
      from the
      history of the fall of the wall, that if it is necessary to use
      that mindset to
      solve it, he felt he ought to point us back there again.

    - The discussion turned to the fact that panel
      2 includes
      coordinates, which fall about 150 feet southeast of the sculpture
      itself.
      Someone asked “How accurate were lat lon coordinates…” at this
      time, being
      before GPS, but no answer came forth.

    - Sanborn mentioned that “something was
      missing” from the
      area around the sculpture, which was there when it was built. He
      was asked how
      important it was to see this, or know what this missing thing was…
      he implied
      it was “important”, but would not say how, or why. Someone asked
      if the panel
      could be solved without it, and he paused, then said, “yes”. This
      made me
      wonder if this could be one of those bronze Geodetic Survey
      Markers, which have
      been placed around by the US government from about the turn of the
      20th
      century. So I asked Elonka, who is a Geocaching expert, how
      accurate the
      positions of these are, considering they were placed long before
      satellite
      navigation. She did not hear my whole question, and answered it in
      relation to
      Geocaching instructions… that those instructions are usually not
      precise, and
      tell you to “Follow a dirt road until the end of the fence, then
      turn on the
      path into the woods…” (that is a rough approximation of her
      answer). So I asked
      again, “No… I mean the bronze markers, placed by the Geodetic
      Survey group…”. I
      think others were answering, and we could not hear each other. But
      interestingly, and perhaps importantly, Sanborn (who was sitting
      about four
      places to my right/front) was looking towards Elonka, and saying,
      “No… the
      bronze markers…”, while holding up his two hands, and making a
      circle with his
      fingers about 3 inches in diameter, clearly demonstrating the size
      of, and
      describing a, Geodetic Survey marker of the type I meant. Was he
      trying to say
      that this was important to his work? Or that this was what was
      missing? Or was
      he simply helping to explain what I meant? In any case, I would
      like to see if
      there was ever a marker like this in the area of the sculpture,
      and  if so, what it had
      written on it… that is,
      serial number? Text? Description? Also, I must look at the
      earliest pictures of
      the Kryptos, to see if this, or some other object (which Sanborn
      might have
      been referring to as gone now), is apparent. Jim Gillogly’s pics
      on Voynich.net
      would be a good start. UPDATE, 11/30/13: I recently
      downloaded the
      geodetic maps of this area, which should show all the bronze
      geodetic survey
      markers in this area. It seems that there were never any of these
      markers
      anywhere near the Kryptos sculpture, or near the CIA headquarters,
      for that
      matter. So the “missing item” must be something other than a
      survey marker.

    - Sanborn expressed surprise that this has
      taken so long. He
      said, “I thought this would be solved in six months, at the
      latest!”. This
      implies the solution may not be so “out there”.

    - I wonder if some speech or text relating to
      the fall of
      the Berlin wall might be used as a “one time pad” sheet for panel
      four. Two
      reasons would be that as Ed implied, “English could not be used…”,
      and use of a
      OTP does, I believe, remove the ability to use word counts in any
      language to
      decipher. Also, Ed explained that the ciphers used were in
      increasingly
      difficult systems… the first three are, leading up to the
      transposition of
      panel 3. It might make sense if panel four is a OTP cipher, which
      are
      indecipherable without the text of the sheet used as a key.

    Update: I looked up the locations of all known
      Geodetic
      markers, and do not believe one has been by the Kryptos. This is
      not certain,
      however… Rich SantaColoma

Here is another set of notes from Rich, this time about our March
    2019 meeting at Sanborn's Studio. Rich's main focus of study is the
    Voynich Manuscript, so I appreciate his fresh viewpoint on the
    Kryptos events. I'm posting his notes in two places, since he
    included a very interesting picture of a pinned (and evidently
    re-pinned) K4 note from Sanborn's desk, which is difficult to
    reproduce here in Yahoogroups. It shows the ciphertext of K4, with
    each letter numbered. Intriguing!

    Richard's full document, with the photo. is available in my Dropbox
    here:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/1ue6g4lc9smtvu4/Personal%20notes%20from%20Rich%20SantaColoma.docx?dl=0

    And the text (making it more searchable) is here:

    ********************************************

    Personal
          notes on
          Kryptos lunch meeting at Jim Sanborn’s gallery on 3/3/19

      Elonka Dunin, along with the film crew of Great Big Story, and Mr.
      Sanborn
      himself, hosted a film shoot and Kryptos meeting at the artist’s
      Maryland
      studio. These pages are my thoughts, observations, and opinions
      from that
      meeting. It is important to realize a few things, though: I am not
      a member of
      the Kryptos Yahoo group, nor other groups related to Kryptos, and
      I have only
      an amateur understanding of cryptology in general. So ideas may
      have been
      mentioned or discussed before, and also, I may have errors and
      misconceptions
      in these observations. Also, any quotes are paraphrased, by me, as
      closely to
      the intent of the speaker as I understood it. They may not be
      fully accurate,
      as they may have been misheard or misunderstood, by me.

    1) “K5”-
      I was
      asking Bob and Denny what they thought of “K5”, which as I
      understood it was
      the possible “cipher within a cipher” of K4, in which some
      secondary cipher
      would reveal a secondary plain text. I was curious about how such
      a thing could
      be done, as it would seem to me to be very difficult to
      accomplish. While Bob
      and Denny were giving their thoughts on this, Jim was listening.
      He suddenly
      said something to the effect of, “What’s this K5 now?”, and when I
      looked over,
      he looked perplexed and maybe a bit bemused. I described the idea
      of what I had
      heard K5 to be, and this got some sort of negative response from
      him. So I then
      offered the possibility that someone, hearing that when K4 is
      deciphered, there
      will “still be a mystery” to solve, had mistaken this to mean
      there was a “K5”
      to be found. This was not disputed by Jim, and so from this
      conversation, I
      took it that there is no K5.

      2) German Guy’s Proposal:
      Elonka
      asked Jim if anyone who guessed through his proposal “system” (the
      $50 a shot
      thing) had come close. At first, Jim said “no”. But then after a
      pause, he said
      something to the effect of, “Well one guy worried me for a
      minute”, or maybe,
      “One got had me scared”, or like that. Elonka asked him to
      elaborate, and he
      said that a German guy had given a “solution” that seemed very
      close at first,
      but then, on (some sort of) further examination, turned out to be
      wrong. So
      this begged the question… and Elonka and I asked in different
      ways… “what”
      about the solution made him think it was wrong, then? The only
      thing I could
      think was that the result was close to correct, but that the method used told Sanborn
      that the result
      was either a lucky guess or happy error. So I asked, specifically,
      after a
      short back and forth, “If a person gave you an answer which was
      100% correct,
      would you care how the person arrived at it?” He answered, firmly,
      “I don’t
      care how they do it”.

      So this brings us back to the German proposal: What about it would
      make Sanborn
      think it correct? And what then would later make him think it
      wrong, if not the
      method used to arrive at it? My friend Greg S. suggested to me, “I
      think you're
      assuming the German sent the whole 'solution' at once. Sanborn
      said there was a
      back-and-forth. I suspect he sent some fragment or query which was
      close enough
      to get Sanborn's interest but on further exchange it turned out to
      be nothing.”
      That makes sense to me, but I mention the exchange because it may
      still be of
      interest. In any case, simply the idea that any solution, partial
      or not, was
      offered to Sanborn, is to me, important. And please don’t think it
      unethical of
      me to suggest that one may think about inquiring of all German
      Kryptos
      researchers and fans, to see who may have sent Sanborn this
      “close” suggestion,
      to find out what that suggestion was. I mean, the $50 requirement,
      along with
      the German clue, could conceivably narrow down the possibilities
      so that this
      person can be found. And anyway, Jim made it clear he does not
      mind how the
      person arrives at the solution. If someone even guessed at some
      portion of the
      solution to K4, knowing that guess could be an immense help to
      solving it.

      3) Times New Roman:
      Elonka asked us
      if we had any questions for Mr. Sanborn, but I really didn’t have
      a specific
      question that I felt appropriate. As I said, I could run my own
      pet ideas about
      what might be going on in K4, trying to elicit a reaction from
      him, but really
      didn’t want to do that. So the best I could do was to ask him what
      font he
      used, and was it Times New Roman. He said he thought it could be
      that, but was
      not positive. He then explained how he marked them out: By
      enlarging an image
      of the letters, then tracing them out with white out (on the
      metal, I
      presumed). Earlier, before everyone arrived, I had asked a
      non-cipher technical
      question about how he physically cut the letters… I had wondered,
      because often
      it is reported that they were cut by water jet, and I felt that
      technology was
      not so prevalent in 1989/90. Jim explained that he cut the letters
      with a Bosch
      “jig saw”… meaning, I took it, a “saber saw” (a jig saw needs
      bottom and top
      attachments for the blade, a saber saw cuts from the top only. The
      terms are
      often interchanged). A side note here: That is extraordinary. The
      work
      involved, to obtain the precision he did, in Kryptos, is really
      astounding… as
      one versed in the use of a Bosch saber saw (although the best one
      out there, we
      both agreed), I can attest to this.

      But there was a further reason for my being interested in Jim’s
      answer to the
      font question: Of course he has stated that the solutions to K1,
      K2 and K3 will
      help with solving K4. But how? There is the possible that the
      plaintext content
      relates, and that of course seems most probable. But I did wonder
      as some sort
      of steganography, using differing fonts, or differences in the
      same fonts, to
      convey meaning: Either in the original order on Kryptos, or, in
      the case of K3,
      the re-order of the plain text solution. So I next asked, “Did you
      use more
      than one font?”. Elonka can correct me, or confirm this, but I do
      not think he
      answered that question. It seemed to me he heard me, but chose not
      to answer.
      If I am correct in this, then it seems the fonts should be pored
      over very
      carefully for any differences. Again, though, being a Kryptos
      neophyte, I can
      only assume many have, already, and I simply don’t know that. I
      only mention
      it… “because”.

      4) K4 Number List:
      Another case of
      my being “certain” that something has been noticed, but still, not
      wanting to
      assume anything: On the board behind Jim’s desk was pinned the
      cipher text of
      K4, but with each letter numbered, 1-97. I would think this was as
      an aid for
      him to quickly explain which characters stand for what, such as
      the number
      range of “BERLIN”, for instance. But its prominence, and
      specialty, I did also
      wonder if it had some other use or significance, and so I mention
      it.

    And not to impart any special importance on
      this
      observation, but that note was taken down and pinned up at least
      two or more
      times, and has seen some use.

      5) “Masking”: I think
      several of us
      noted, as did I, that Jim seemed a bit confused by Ed Scheidt’s
      use of the term
      “masking”. This came up at least a couple of times, most notably
      when Denny
      asked about it, and whether “BERLIN CLOCK” was masked first, or
      part of the
      plain text, or some intermediate step, and so on. I noted… sure
      everyone did…
      that Jim and Ed looked to each other to try and figure out a way
      to both
      understand and explain the “masking” claim. I sensed… may be
      wrong, but I
      sensed… that Jim didn’t know what Ed meant about “masking” K4.

    6)
        Digital vs. Analog:
      Ed had, in several personal discussions both at Elonka’s, and at
      the studio,
      reiterated his passion for historical analog cipher methods and
      solutions. From
      what he said, it added to my belief that K4 IS something that can
      be solved
      “paper and pencil”, using clues and information contained in
      K1-K3, just as
      they also could be.

      7) “Matrices”: Jim was
      explaining,
      on at least two occasions, his passion for matrices. But he was
      also
      discussing, using hand gestures, “rotating” them, and I think (?)
      “flipping” or
      “mirroring” them (could be wrong on those last two). As a noobie
      to this, and
      not being a cipher expert, I mention it because I am not sure that
      “rotating”
      the matrices was a part of the solved K1-K3. If not, then I would
      say this is
      some sort of possible suggestion, because he was stating it in
      relation to
      these panels, perhaps a further way to glean another layer of
      information from
      them? Yeah, not strong… but again, mentioned “because”.

      My Conclusions: I don’t
      really have
      anything earth-shaking to offer, only the above observations and
      opinions in
      the rare chance they may be of interest or use to others. Overall,
      I did note
      that Jim seems a bit frustrated that K4 has not been solved, as he
      is so well
      known for it, and of course has “moved on” to other art styles,
      other
      techniques, long since then. For this reason I would assume that
      the last clue,
      which he says will come this year, may be very revealing.

    Rich SantaColoma, March 6, 2019

    proto57.wordpress.com, youtube.com/proto57,
      voynich.net,
      [courriel]

Thanks for sending that along.

It's not gonna happen that somebody stumbled on it, so there's more misdirection in having people think they can be lucky. Having said that, if you think Stein's account was long, you ain't seen nothin' yet. Yes, this is all haughty talk from one person among all others who haven't solved K4 yet.

s: Request for Sunday Kryptos notes (& some stuff of my own)
t:
And thank you for having us down..  Makes a nice break from Vermont in the latter end of winter, tho the slog up the Jersey Pike in a snowstorm on the way back brought me home a little earlier than I cared for.

Heard 2 things from Ed Scheidt. For one, he mentioned the idea of a prism as being useful.  As he did not elaborate, I take it he was comparing a masking layer to a piece of glass which takes in a mixture of light wavelengths and splits them into the different components of white light.  I can't say I'd ever looked at it quite that way, but it doesn't tell me anything new about what a masking layer does.  It's not an all-fours metraphor, as the prism differentiates the spectrum based on the specific characteristics of the wavelength mix put into it; a masking layer, so far as I can understand it, specifically ignores the values input, and "bends the colors", so to speak, into a variegated output which has as little relation to the input as can be managed.  Anyway, I did understand that statement to have been in relation to Kryptos-cracking.

For the other, much of which also heard by Rich Santacoloma, he was interested in bases.  Why do we operate on base 10, what other bases might others devise/use, &c.  (Analog CLOCKs use base 12, is that what, if anything Kryptos-related, he was getting at?)  Also problems of achieving coordination among nations working on digital currencies, &c., much the same as he was on about in 2017.  Anybody's guess whether it subtly relates to Kryptos or is deflection therefrom.

Having been reinvigorated in my Kryptos endeavors, I set to work to clear up a couple small items before digging into 'trying all the shifts' of the 281-digit string I have been on about for the last year and a half.  Namely:  At K1#56 & #57 we have an overt 'error' and at least the suggestion of a subtle one.  An allusion, say to Woodrow Wilson, has as much nuance as an illusion.  I propose that K1#56  'should' rightly have been an "a", and that this possibility directs our attention to it.  After all, we are given an unexpected 'cue', aren't we?  So, let us look at these two as ordinal number & Factors:  56&3x19  It occurred to me to be sure that I was doing what I should in dividing 19 by 563, and not perhaps multiplying them as this view of things would indicate.  Behold, 563x19=10697, thus also fulfilling the instructions at K2/K3 "Layer 2 end, ID by row's end".  I now think 10697 is the more likely basis for the masking layer as it would be far easier for encoder and decoder to deal with.  Of its 5 possible positions, I would lean toward the fourth, 97106, as this would give it an ID at either end of the mask you care to grab ([19 x 5] + 2 = 97, so the full mask in the 4th position would be 9710697106 ... 1069710697), thus satisfyingly artistically balanced.  Also indicated (???) by the 45 of YA in K3 hinting 4' place out of 5 for the mask?  Or might the 45 hint that 4/5 of the letters are masked, and 1/5 only as the 'classic cryptography' hides them?  (And the 7 for the kee BERLINP?)

While the 281-digit string also has various numbers that might identify it as what's wanted (e.g., 19/563 starts out 337...), the K1#56&#57-derived number contains at its "row's end" the specific 97 of K4.  The 281-digit string had the drawback that it would have required the encoder to divide some number by 563 out to about 290 places or so.  As Kryptos is an objet-d'art and K4 is not necessarily a practical field cipher, and the anamath was aided by the mathematician in the design, that might not greatly matter, but it is a point against it.  Using 10697 for the basis (I am assuming simply repeated 19 times with some 2 of its digits added at the end) plenty of complexity could be added for security's sake by quite simple algorithms if that were wanted; you don't have to give up a lot of security in swapping 281 for 5 in the basis for the mask.

Although I would now favor 10697 over 0017761989.....373 to derive the mask, for reasons of simplicity & reduced chance for error, I have not given up entirely on the latter.  563 is pretty nearly a given; it is thrown at us in many places by the sculpture and is needed to derive either of these two numbers for a mask basis.  I must admit that I have never found a hint saying "divide" that is nearly as straightforwardly convincing (to me anyway) as is the hint saying "multiply" described above.  On the other hand, 844 remains 563+281, and the T in K3 at the end of the only 33-letter line on the sculpture is still at K3/281, and there is no use that I have found for 281 if it is not pointing to the 281-digit string obtained by dividing some integer by 563.  I am nearly back to believing that one or the other of these things is a deliberately planned decoy.  But I had rather work on 4 shifts than 280.  Surely, if I need unnecessary aggravation, there will be shifts of the keyword, shifts of the (possible) matrix, &c.  Altho - I must enjoy unnecessary aggravation, or why am I doing this at all?  :)

I wish we knew just who did just what on this thing.  I believe the quote re English-language stats was approximately "you don't have access to that, because I masked it".  As reported, the pronoun is "I", not "We", not "He", and the speaker was Ed.  I'm sure Jim is up to basic +-x&/ arithmetic but it would be really nice to know how much of what Ed handed him with "here, for that, just use this the way I showed you" and what Jim had to work out for himself.  You can't get BERLINPEEKRRR found in K4 by using the first 11 letters of K1, and ENDJAHR at the beginning of K3 (after precise redaction of Carter), without some rather tricky procedures.  Not that bad, but probably not Jim's cup of tea.  So who actually wrote the passages, anyhow?

Wilson Primes - all now accounted for:

5 - for the length of the mask basis

13 - for the letters BERLINPEEKRRR & for WoodrowWilson.  And as a factor of a matrix of 676 letters?

563 - for the multiplier to obtain those 5 masking digits

-Carl Ellis

s: Wondrous Patterns: Puzzles: X LAYER TWO, DY A HR, ENCEOF, DQM and SIBLE
t:
So, while keeping my information gathering in the back burner and limiting myself to creating a 24-column grid spreadsheet with paired ciphertext / plaintext, I came across some other interesting things that appear to give a starting point of clues outside of straight cipher-solving.

Three of the first were repeated cipher strings in K1 and K2 that matched repeated plain strings.

K1 – VJYQT=NCEOF

K2 – GWHKK= SIBLE and DQM = THE

There’s another in K2 (NUVP) that I haven’t gotten to yet..

That SIBLE sticks out for a couple reasons.

Basic rot+1 rot-1 cipher with a ct/pt pairing that is inferred from the misspellings at K3

D+1 = E

Y/L (DES PAR AT LY)

A+1 = B

H+1 = I

R+1 = S

Noting that, and adding in Jim’s comments about not using the English language, I consider phonics (NCEOF=FONEC?) and got a great result = SIBYL, and reference to an ancient greek word for the prophetesses at oracular locations. I’ll spare you how the individual details of those 10+ women fit into my background research, because there’s only one that’s of special interest here: The Erythrean Sibyl. This Sibyl was the first known historical example of using Acrostics, otherwise known as Null Ciphers, based on the way she spelled words in her prophecies written on leaves….

Acrostics, though – for those interested, I’m referring to T IS AST BALLOON, T IS FLOWING ROBES, T IS HROHNL and the ISTANBUL acrostic from former discussions.

Now the process is starting to make a lot more sense and lead from Point A to Point Z.

~ James

--

Inside of a dog it is too dark to read."
G. Marx

however, a significant number of electrons were inconvenienced.)

s: Kryptos: Kasiski Analysis Theory, Puzzles & Multi-layering
t:
Theory: Like DY A HR, the misspellings and other known elements, the patterns found by a Kasiski examination also provide not just the means to crack the code, but secondary clues as well.  Kasiski, that is seeking repetitions in ciphertext and their accompanying repeated plaintext.  Carefully selected  repetitions should carry an extra layer of meaning. These are, in order: ENCEOF, SIBLE, THE, IGHT

Decoding K1 grants solver ENCEOF, which deciphers as FONEC/PHONIC.

Applying PHONIC to visible ct SLLSLLNOHSNOS, you get WW KNOWS/NOSE/NOS

Decoding K2.1 grants SIBLE, a phonic to SIBYL.

Apply SIBLE to visible ct, solver finds that DY A HR = ELBIS, a backward rot+1 with a wildcard.

Decoding K2.2 grants THE. This has no immediately apparent context.

Decoding K2.3 grants IGHT, also with no immediately apparently context.

The SIBYL is associated with the acrostic aka null cipher, that is divined from the words made from letters at the beginning of rows. ID BY ROWS begins to apply here.

Apply SIBYL acrostic to K1 "Between Subtle…. Etc" yields T IS AST BALLOON.

Apply flattened plaintext of K1-K2 to K3-K4 in rows. There is no immediately apparent clue for twenty four. This comes from Sanborn’s notes. The "FAR ROWS" yield acrostics, left & right.

Applying SIBYL acrostic to K2-Left yields T IS FLOWING ROBES

Applying SIBYL acrostic to K3-Left yields T IS HROHNL

Applying SIBYL acrostic to K1-Left & K1-K3 Right yields FR ISTANBUL WATCHTOWER SESTOS XANTH FLBL.

Conclusion: There may be further unfound items by looking more closely at K3 as well.

Advanced, "wrapping" and misspellings.

Apply UNDERGRUUN (DOUBLE-U/W)  to DES PAR AT LY with SIBYL/DYAHR reversal = DES WRAP AT LY

While examining  the TEW/DRY in K1, there is an emphasis on a piece of the IQLUSION text that expands into K2. The takeaway from this WRAP effect suggests K1-K2 at the very least, and probably K1-k4 are all a singular document. Applying…

"BETWEEN SUBTLE SHADING AND ABSENCE OF LIGHT LIES THE NUANCE OF IQLUS (Eye Clues) ||| ION (EYE ON)  IT WAS TOTALLY INVISIBLE. HOWS THAT POSSIBLE?"

"X LAYER TWO SLOWLY. DES WRAP AT LY Y. SLOWLY THE REMAINS OF PASAGE DEBRIS…."

Conclusion: K4 may wrap the same way. "CAN YOU SEE ANY? THING Q" (THINK)

~ James

s: Wondrous Patterns: THE-NCEOF-SIBLE-IGHT, Phonics and Raphael
t:
Phonic assembly:
THE INKER OF VISIBLE LIGHT

Raphael is famous for painting "Sibyls" a unique work featuring four of the Sibyls of Greek history..  Aside from its parallels to Michaelangelo’s Sistine work this painting has an interesting feature – there is a half-circle cut out of the lower half of it, giving the appearance of statues in its depth and the Sibyls and Angels painted on it are given the illusion of sitting or flying above a hill. This is an important concept because Sibyls supposedly didn’t just receive messages from the gods, but could see beyond into the underworld. There’s a striking parallel to the Kryptos exhibit in this: the half-circle hill above in the courtyard, the subterranean facility below the courtyard, with a pool between, which Sibyls are storied for scrying through. HYDRA, of course, features into the mythology as one of the incorporeal beasts of the underworld when Aeneas is guided by a Sibyl.

All those neat parallels aside, this links both to the acrostic keys  and another one of Raphael’s paintings, the ascension of Christ in "Transfiguration", with many aspects that could be presented as "visible light", the painting itself a subject I’ve gone over with the "T=TRANS" posts, completing the circle.

 Conclusion: It seems likely that undiscovered clues are supposed to build upon either the acrostics or the Transfiguration concept when coupled with K3 in order to get to understanding how to decode K4.

RAY as a play on Raphael?

~ James

s: Wondrous Patterns: Puzzle - Sibyls and Elonka’s Markers, Codex Aureus
t:
Clarification: "Wondrous Patterns" is an attempt to analyze Kryptos based strictly on a procession of clues within the sculpture itself, the previous body of research acting as a body of "intelligence gathering" to support and understanding of the clues in it.

On Elonka’s recent visit to Langley, she noted something that had not been noticed before: a half circle of slotted  bronze markers around the Kryptos exhibit at roughly 15 foot intervals. If you’ve seen a bird’s eye view of the courtyard, it’s already obvious that there’s a half circle surrounding the duck pond, apparently on a hill. The bronze markers  reinforce that concept at the level of someone on site. I’d speculated that this seems very similar to the idea of a directional circle, and wondered if this was what Sanborn had been referring to when he said the bronze marker was "missing". Could it be that when he was asked about it, the coordinates as people understood them began from the wrong location and Sanborn didn’t pick up on that?

That idle guessing aside, this half-circle correlates directly to Raphael’s "SIBYLS" with it’s half-circle, dial-like center. If you haven’t seen the picture, it’s four of the Sibyls surrounding the half-circle (cut out portion of the painting). They are the Cumaen, Phrygian, Persian and Tiburtine Sibyls, a few of the many, attended by the angels giving them secret prophecies from above, some partly revealed on finally detailed parchments in the portrait such as a piece of "I AM". This bit is of note.

Identifying the Sibyls is a bit of a task, but apparently Raphael is noted for modeling his Sibyls after those of Michaelangelo in the Sistene Chapel, giving images to work with. Michaelangelo’s painted five of the Sibyls who supposedly foretold the Coming of Christ. With those models it’s possible to clearly identify a couple of the Sibyls. If we apply the K2 coordinates, it appears to point to the Persian Sibyl.

The Persian Sibyl is noted for foretelling the Coming of Alexander the Great AND the coming of Christ. This is particularly interesting because of the number of characters in K3 – 336. This is a unique date in it’s dichotomy of BC vs AD. In 336 BC, Alexander the Great inherited Macedonia and began his famed campaign, while in 336 AD. More to the point of the puzzle, is the Christ side of the equation, as noted also in Raphaels' Transfiguration.

PALIMPSEST - old ground with the purple vellum parchments of the Codex Aureus of St Emmerman. To the point: The cover of this codex has a striking arrangement similar to Kryptos, a square divided into four parts by an axis, with each square containing a picture of Christ’s Miracles. The center of the picture is (illusion of paint?) superimposed with a portrait of Christ in Majesty at the center.

Conclusion:  If Kryptos is a visual metaphor for the Codex cover, might that suggest that the four central corners, 24 characters apiece with L in the center, represent some sort reversible alphabet for the K4 ciphertext?

~ James

s: Wondrous Patterns: DYAHR/SIBLE, Raphael and Codex Aureus
t:
When I saw the Kryptos-like pattern on the
Codex Aureus of St Emmerman, I speculated that it could be an implication of a
K3-like clue or a One Time Pad. The former is far simpler, so I started
there.  If you've not read this already, SIBLE is the reversed rot+1 of
DYAHR with L as a wildcard. SIBLE is important because it's a pattern
repetition in K2 and is part of the Kasiski Method cryptanalysis of Vigenere.
I've also been treating these cyptanalytic methods as a clue in themselves,
something laid down by Jim Sanborn to look back at after solving K1-K3 and use
to break K4.

   So, with that first puzzle in mind, I
applied similar tactics here, choosing 5x5 above and below with the central L,
with the center on my 35x14 Plaintext Grid of K1-K4, far right row. Result.

R E E S F

P O I N T

E N T Y S

U T E S F

X L A Y E

     L

G E D E B

E L O W E

S R E M O

D S I M A

P P E R L

    I thought route
transposition cipher at first, since it had some immediately apparently
elements that relate to Raphael’s Sibyl’s portrait, didn’t seem like byproducts
of plaintext and called to mind a route transposition cipher. I discarded the
latter as a broken idea, and went for phonetic anagramming instead.

SEREF

POINT

TYNES

F(L)UTES

YAXLE

More plainly – SEREF POINT
FLUTE’S TYNES (at) Y-AXLE

In Raphael’s portrait, that’s
an immediately obvious reference to the seraphim advisor sitting at the top of
the half-circle, pointing his flute downward into what seems to be the
Underworld… which I hadn’t realized IS actually a very SUBTLE part of the
painting, not a cut-out. What he’s pointing at is a pair of reversed twin
seraphims on top a very sharp V-point, which if lined up with that flute,
creates a neat Y.

Not so much about the
coordinates, I don’t think as what they represent – the Underworld.

Which seems to be
represented in the bottom half of this puzzle, but I haven’t worked out yet
what’s going on with it. It appears to refer to the Underworld also, possibly from
Homer’s Odyssey (OMERS DSI) which has a journey through the Underworld.

Their underworld is
notably inhabited by the likes of Hydra and Scylla of Scylla and Charybdis fame.
For those not familiar with the mythology, that’s a pair of monsters in the
form of a Whirlpool and a Six-Headed creature between which a ship must try and
pass safely.

Conclusion: A metaphor
for the Kryptos whirlpool and rock benches? Perhaps where the light comes
through to form words on the pavement?

s: Wondrous Patterns: THE MIST X, EMU/UME and the Underworld
t:
Small puzzle, big results.
   T IS HROHNL is one of the acrostics from the Sibyl puzzle, and seems to be the natural follow-up to Puzzle 3. I applied the rot+1 from DYAHR=SIBLE and phonetic concepts from Puzzle 3.HROHNL = ISPIOM = I (SPY) OM

   Utilizing the 35x14 plaintext grid as reference, it’s immediately notable that OM is the beginning of a line in a key location. Specifically that’s the OM just before “THE MIST X CAN YOU SEE ANYTHING Q”

I SPY: THE MIST X + phonetics = THE M IS STYX

  A HUGE clue. I’ve speculated that there are elements of Kryptos that refer to the ciphers used and the cipher needed to solve K4. This seems to be it.

 The Styx is popularly presented as a river, but in mythology it is actually a marsh, that is a QUAGMIRE. One of the paths from it leads to Tartarus in which stands a Tower of Iron….. encircled by a bronze fence and great pillars, that is COLUMNS, and guarded by an erinyes in bloody robes. The gates of the palatial Tartarus itself are guarded by the hydra.

   Quagmire Vigenere, to my understanding, is the cipher used to decrypt K1 to K2, and if M = Styx, this explains EMU/UME beginning at K1’s first line and ending at K2’s last line. EM,U = Styx, Underworld.  Keyed columnar transposition is used to solve K3.

Conclusion: T = TOWER? If K1-K2 are Styx and K3 is Tartarus, this might mean that K4 is the unbreakable Tower of Iron. This might be an explanation for the mysterious “folds” indicated on Sanborn’s handwritten notes – a reminder that the edges are folded to create a cylindrical “Tower”.

James

s: Wondrous Patterns: TISIPHONE/T IS IPHONE and The Aeneid.
t:
I have been trying to draw a complete picture from the SIBYL puzzle without expecting to have actual pictures associated with them. The SIBYL clues were these:

T IS AST BALLOON (rising hot air balloon)

T IS FLOWING ROBES (common garment in greek paintings)

T IS HROHNL (phonetic throne cryptogram)

   Now that I’ve found Styx and Tartarus with its parallels to the puzzle, another item suddenly pops out. Styx is the quagmire surrounding Tartarus, the city of the dead with it’s columns, and part of it is a giant and unbreakable Turret/Tower of iron. That’s notable for K4, but more interesting is its guardian An Erinyes/Fury clad tasked with driving familial murderers to madness, she is clad in blood wet flowing robes, wielding a great whip at the top of the tower. This relates to the painting I mentioned: The Fury Tisiphone at the Palace of Athamas. Depicted is the Fury, clad in her FLOWING ROBES  and FLOATING above the ground, confronting a patricidal king upon his THRONE. Her POSITION is above and to the right of him, at a similar angle to the coordinates.

   Her name is  TISIPHONE – T IS IPHONE. I

   Ignoring the iphone element, that’s a neat combination of T IS theme and literal association with phonetics, the sort of play on names that is excellent to incorporate for clues not terribly different from a SIBYL and her acrostics/ACROSS STYX, as she leads the hero Aeneas on the journey through the Underworld to Tartarus, a journey illustrated and written of by Raphael and Vergil.

Conclusion? TISIPHONE or perhaps TISPHONE may be a K4 keyword.

~ James

So, my “big idea” for Kryptos is that I think Jim Sanborn created a new method of encryption for K4 by doing both methods that he knew: a Vigenère cipher first and then rearranging the letters second. In other words, I think Sanborn did a K1/K2 and then a K3.

However, I think that maybe Sanborn rearranged the tiles in some new way however he felt like it. For example, maybe he did something like this going across and then down:

T
HI
SIS
ASEC
RETME
SSAGEX

|
V V
| | V
V V | |
| | V V |

= THSARSIISESSETACMGEEX

My theory is that Sanborn is an artist and thinks visually, and would not be able to resist shuffling the tiles in some unusual geometric fashion and calling that “encryption”.

To test my idea, I wrote a Python program to reverse the steps I think Sanborn took:

To encrypt:
K1: Do a Vigenère
K3: Shuffle the tiles

To decrypt:
K3: Shuffle the tiles
K1: Do a Vigenère

My program randomly mixes the 97 letters of K4, and then does a reverse Vigenère with every word of a UNIX dictionary with the result. Then, the 64th to 74th letters are compared to BERLINCLOCK to see how many letters match up.

I’ve been running my code 12 hours a day since October 2018 (using PythonAnywhere.com) and I’ve come up with many shuffles/keywords that match 8 out of the 11 letters in BERLINCLOCK, and a few shuffles/keywords that match 9 out of 11 letters, but none that match 10 or all 11.

See the uploaded file "PatrickKellogg_Keyword20190320.txt" for the keyword list so far.
