s: Baudot Codes, negating, mirroring and clues
t:
Its funny I pulled myself back into Kryptos again. My brain is quickly overloaded. But, I refreshed my memory of where I left off in 2014.

I wanted to talk again about the relationship of certain letters when using Baudot international codes in digital form.

The 5 digit binary code for each letter can be mirrored or negated  or both into other letters. (i.e. "A" can be mirrored to "O", negated to "M", or mirrored and negated to "U". There are only 3 pairs of letters that have unique relationship of the code that only transform to each other, and that is XQ, YR, and CZ

The interesting thing about X and Q in Baudot is they are mirrors of each other
 X = 10111 and Q = 11101

and YR (which is the morse code RQ read upside down) are negates of each other. (Maybe YR was the intended meaning of that morse code)

Y = 10101 and R = 01010

I don't know or remember any particular clue point to CZ unless someone can refresh my memory

if you look at other clues from the misspelling of undergruund , O to a U

O = 00011 and U= 11100 which are negatives of each other.

This can lead to certain suggested operands to be used, and maybe those were clues telling to use those operands Mirroring and Negating the baudot codes of cipher text into Plain text.

My analysis led to several operands using that to find a relationship between NYPVTTMZFPK to BERLINCLOCK, also with some shifting of positions. Maybe I just forced it to make it work, but they started to appear to be a pattern that I couldn't ever really crack totally.

However, some weird words did start to form that I thought was interesting back then. I started to get the word "perpetual bulb" several characters before the text "berlin clock". I did a search on this, and sure enough the creator of the Berlin Clock was working on some type of perpetual bulb that would prevent him from having to change the bulbs in the clock so often. This was way too weird for that to be a lucky coincidence.

Maybe when Sanborn said you better delve into that clock, I don't think he meant using the mechanisms of the clocks as a solution method, but rather the solution itself can be more about the clock and what was trying to be created: The perpetual bulb, which I think was controversial at the time.

Anyway, I cant retrace how exactly I came up with the letters that brought out the words perpetual bulb, but it was along the lines of using 5 digit baudot codes and performing negates, mirrors and shifts of positions.

Hi all,

I know that a few of us, like myself, are amateurs (or less) in cryptography and cryptanalysis so I thought I’d share some of the more intriguing reading I’ve come across while researching my angles on Kryptos.

First and foremost is a fantastic, insightful book by Helen Fouche Gaines called Cryptanalysis: A study of ciphers and their solutions. Despite it’s age (1939!) it’s a nice primer on some of the ciphers nearest and dearest to Kryptos, such as Quagmire Vigenere and transpositions and of course a number of others. I have to appreciate it for that. Coming in at this as a novice, I see a great deal of emphasis on two of the three major classifications: Substitution and Transposition ciphers with all their many variants, without a lot of mention of
the third, Concealment ciphers. Playing this from the rank amateur side, I have to wonder if that’s what Scheidt and Sanborn really mean in referring to "masking".
   There’s a lot to like, and even some elementary ciphers to play with, but beware the rather small print that seems to be a byproduct of its time. Can be kind of hard to read without keen eyesight.

On the CIA side, there’s also a fun 2015 read called The Billion Dollar Spy by Pulitzer prize winner David Hoffman, a non-fiction work about the background story surrounding the Tolkachev/Edward Lee Howard spy swap in the 80s. Apparently it was such a notable incident that Tolkachev even got his own painting in the CIA. Fascinating  history about turncoats that would have been recent history in Sanborn’s time. No direct relevance to Kryptos otherwise, so far as I can tell.

Enjoy!

s: Wondrous Patterns: The Three Judges Puzzle, Rotations and Europa
t:
In Greek mythology, Tartarus is an inverted dome, a cosmic half-spheric underworld to the other half in the heavens above. Sentencing of the dead to Tartarus comes at the PLAIN/PLANE of Judgment, at the hands of the judges Rhadymanthus, Aiakos and Minos. The former two are responsible for judging the souls of Asians and Europeans respectively, while Minos is BINARY, judging those cases that are undecided.

  I’ve been fiddling with Turning Grille logic as applied to various formations and stumbled on what looks to be another puzzle, that being the Three Judges aligned along the first line of K3’s ABSCISSA. Their positions are as such:

The Three Judges Puzzle

RHADY = DYAHR

AIAKOS = Extreme left of line one, AIA visible in ciphertext, KOS hidden by the Tableau. Meangingful.

MINOS is hidden in an alternating rotation scheme  at ROHNL. H is repeated and nixed. L is morse for T:

Apply a positive/negative rotation pattern of +1/-1.

R+1= S

O-1= N

H+1= I

N-1 = M

T+1= U

=MINUS/MINOS

This covers all three judges, but one has a special role – AIAKOS holds the KEYS to Tartarus and is the judge of the European dead. European as in Europa mother of Tartarus or Europa Center, a place of a number of BERLIN CLOCKS. This appears to be a first internal clue leading to BERLIN in general, if not clock rotation, independent of Jim Sanborn that leads there.

Take a look at the grid and you’ll see something interesting in alignment: the AIA rows in ciphertext directly precede the BER and LIN rows hidden in plaintext. A stretch? Maybe, but there’s some equally interesting  things going on when comparing rotations.

Conclusion? AIAKOS may be some kind of key that acts as a turning mechanism in rotation.

~ James

s: Wondrous Patterns: TEW/DRY and the Flaming River Puzzle
t:
After noting the +1/-1 repeating pattern on MINOS in the "Three Judges" puzzle, I decided to try that as a tactic on the K3 letters between TEW/DRY. Because of the Greek Underworld theme, and the way it crosses to Styx, I already had an inkling of where it might go.

    I'll upload a companion document to illustrate later, but you can achieve the same thing by using the DDs in the formation to create the end of a pair of lines, split roughly half between 39 letters. The first row is 20 letters, the second is 19. It's easiest on an Excel spreadsheet. Circle the first four alternating letters in each line. Note the SIT in the second line and circle the T. Note the W in the first line and circle it.

Using UNDERGRUUND/UNDER-GR-UU (W)-ND and use that as a substitution for W=N.

Your circled letters anagram to PHLEGETHON and are transmitted under the DD "ends" Taking note of the SIT, you have a T-I-S PHLEGETHON. There's almost enough for RIVER as well, but I can't identify the logic behind it.  The word is enough to identify it as the underworld Greek god of the flaming river.

Conclusion: WET/YRD suggests the cute wet feet-dry feet call sign except getting one's feet wet in QUAGMIRE, while drying them off in the Flaming River. What more to take from that, I'm still working on.

~ James

s: Wondrous Patterns = Clock Puzzle - The Hidden BER-LIN = NYPVT in K3
t:
As noted before, I’m working on a 35x24 flattened Grid of plaintext, allowing me to pick up patterns that aren’t as obvious in the ciphertext.  I’ve noticed and had on backburner an obvious pattern of BER and LIN aligned in the same three columns, one row apart. After filling out the rest of K3, something else suddenly stuck out.
  Following BER to LIN to the bottom, the bottom of K3 ends with NYO(the letters in can you see anything). The immediate three letters after it turn it into an odd rot+1 pattern like in the DYAHR/SIBLE rot+1 puzzle.

N=N

Y=Y

O+1=P

U+1=V

S+1=T

This is a visual trick The highlighted formation of BER and LIN forms an EQUAL sign (note misspellings).

BERLIN = NYPVT

Conclusion: Special note goes to the fact that Jim Sanborn gave us NYPVTT – K3 gives us NYPVT only… six letters corresponding to five. What the take away is from this, I’m not quite sure. I'm also not clear on how this pattern matches up to the Underworld Theme.

~ James

s: Wondrous Patterns: The Berlin Puzzle, "T" and Kryptos.
t:
I renamed this from The Clock Puzzle to the Berlin Puzzle to partition Jim’s outside clues from the process of discovery I’m using. This puzzle seems to center on columns 13-15 on my Plaintext flattened grid, and while there’s a superficial resemblance to the 3-column  Berlin-to-Istanbul of the World Clock, it’s not enough for me to call it clock.

Columns 13-15:

~ All misspellings fall within these columns. –ION  -NDT  -SPA

~ The "T" formation from –OIN intersecting with DESPAR falls within the columns

~ BER- and –LIN are on alternating columns in these rows. There’s even a neat HINT in the row after.

~ NY-OUS falls on the final line of K3 in these columns. NY-OUS=NYPVT at a masked rot+1

Takeaways:

~ BER and LIN line up in a neat "EQUAL" pattern, matching up to the misspellings specific letters. Result? BERLIN = NYPVT in previous notes.

~ ION-NDT-SPA seems to have something as well… EYE ON END. T IS PA.  Put their FULL words together and you have ILLUSION/UNDERGROUND/DESPARATLY/ENCUMBERED/TREMBLING..

In context of Tartarus, that’s meanginful as the Titan Atlas, father of Dione/Aphrodite, he who holds the celestial sphere upon his shoulders as punishment. Since Tartarus is the lower half of the celestial sphere, he’s technically not IN it, but holding it.

Conclusion: The "Eye" on the back of Kryptos represents Atlas, and the quarter-sphere UNDERGROUND in K2 represents a piece of that celestial sphere. Thereotically, this means there may be meaning in tracing out the entire sphere on Kryptos. It also seems to suggest that a lot of the "puzzles" I've come across are meant to act as markers to a set path.

~ James

Hi,

I am a Kryptos fan with some math and it background. I have decided to share something that I think is quite interesting and something that I haven`t seen anywhere else.

It will be a bit long, so tldr: I hope that TURING will be the next clue.

A little bit of history of Kryptos and me.

I have started my journey with Krypots in 2014 - I just read somewhere about the CLOCK clue (I think it was something similar to "top 10 unsolved mysteries"). I decided to give it a try - just to learn something new and get back into programming.

First attempts were focused on simple ideas, exchanged with months of breaks. I remember trying:
- Vigenere ciphers based on ABC alphabet and all words from dictionary
- I think I also tried Vigenere based on all alphabets based on words from the dictionary and all words as an encryption key
- simple additions based on two keys (decrypted_message + key1key1key1... + key2key2key2...)
- I even tried to use genetic algorithms to try to find some interesting local strings of words

Then I stopped using such algorithms and started to think: "Were I Mr. Sanborn, how would I do it". Assumptions were:
- cipher that could be used on paper
- cipher that an artist would understand
- cipher that would use keys connected to Kryptos
- cipher that would be composed of more than 1 step

After some trials I`ve finally found an approach that using some of obvious keys together with K1-K3 would give clear passage from BC -> NYP...
That was interesting since a couple of other patterns occured AFTER I found this approach.
Nevertheless, it was too complicated. I`ve analyzed it a bit more and (not seeing a simple way of extrapolating it on other positions of K4) stopped analysing this approach.

Then I have added additional assumptions:
- it must not be easily solvable by computers
- the algorithm for K4 needs to have a room for another message (K5)

This was the moment when I`ve rewritten everything to other computing language and used additoinal ML/AI for text processing.
That was interesting. That was the time where I found really interesting pattern - it was based strictly on BC->NYP... clue and nothing more.

Again, AFTER that more things started to occur, there was YAR clearly visible, there was iQlusion, undergrUund, despAratly - all of them also very interesting.
I thought that I must be one step before the end, yet I could not reach it. This was the time I have found and analyzed old tables that Mr. Sanborn shared. These were Palimpsest, Abscissa and K3 tables. This was the time when IQlusion got my attention. I looked at these tables and my remark was that:
- either Mr. Sanborn made a mistake with C - look how awful "S" in PALIMPSEST is written there, below the ILLUSION word.. Even in the PALIMPSEST phrase at the top - it reminds the phrase: PALIMPCEST not PALIMPSEST. Maybe when Mr. Sanborn has already cut the letters in the sculpture it was too late to correct it - so he decided to use it somehow as a clue, or just did not see it
- or other way - Mr. Sanborn planned it from the beginning

I remember from some records, that Mr. Sanborn once told something about these typos being "intentional" so I believed the second part.

Then more extraordinary patterns occured - really interesting. Seeing them and seeing other various possibilities of how to further use the pattern that occured in BC to NYP... many further ways of analysis occured, to many paths to follow for one person. This was the time when I decided to share all of it. But I decided to do it my way and I started to do so.

(Un-)fortunately the meeting with Mr Sanborn occured - the movie-making ground for new documentary. I have read the notes and remark about "Q" in an Illusion (meaning that it probably is just a mistake), the BC -> NYP... "in place" algorithm and other remarks. They all disappointed me a bit. After all of that I decided again to give it a try one more time and changed a bit the assumptions.

Before I continue I must say, that I think that if I were the sculpture creator and made any mistake - I would certainly clearly say what is a mistake and what is not.

Coming back to the sculpture.
After taking into consideration new assumptions more new doors opened. This was the time when I loosened the assumptions and took the most wide possibility to follow:
1) reverse the pattern that I found for all positions on K4
2) look for 2-word phrases (instead of just long words)

I think that it was very interesting. One of such "possible" phrases, is really interesting. I have written about it in "Python, Turing and Kryptos" post. It was really interesting since it produces ALAN TURING words - using the same approach as for BC. What is more interesting, the same approach produces more interesting phrases. E.g. LETCHLEY PARK in another place.

Why are these phrases interesting?
As for Turing - there is only one place where TURING word comes in K4 after reversing the application of the pattern (the same one as for BC), and ALAN word comes directly near the TURING word.

The LETCHLEY PARK was found a bit different way: I thought that it would be interesting to analyze the PARK word further. There is also only one place where it is possible after applying the "reversed pattern" approach. Then I decided to check if BLETCHLEY could be obtained before this word. Unfortunately not whole BLETCHLEY word can be obtained. Only LETCHLEY. Either it is a coincidence or something needs to be changed in the algorithm.
I think that it should be analyzed further.

There are also two other possibilities that occur after reversing the pattern that I want to share.
One is the name of the machine used for decryption process during WW2.
The second one was " CYPHER" phrase - also used during WW2, directly connected to the machine above.

Coming back to the previous year. I made a decision to share all my knowledge about Kryptos. Like I said - I wanted to do it my way.
Unfortunately, from other perspective, I think that it probably would be better to wait for the next clue (that will occur this year) and verify whether my approach is consistent with it or not.

Coming back to the "tldr" message.
I hope, that the next clue will be released in June and it will be the TURING word. I believe that the CLOCK clue was released, because of the time when the movie about Mr. Turing had its premiere.

I must say that I have enough of Kryptos - especially because of the mistakes. I really do not want to look at K4 anymore (but I admit that I sometimes do - e.g. that happened after the last interview with Mr. Sanborn).

To summarize: using the phrase at the beginning: "something that I haven`t seen anywhere else" from the beginnig of my post. What I meant was that I think that:

BLETCHLEY PARK
 CYPHER

TURING ALAN

are used inside K4.
I have sorted them by the first letter, not by the occurance in the K4. I hope it is not a coincidence.

Best regards,
Greg

btw. look for Muko and Amartia - that was my plan of sharing my current knowledge (as in 2018)

s: A Coincidence Between two unsolved mysteries
t:
Hi Yahoo Groups,

I had an idea to solve part K4 of Kryptos. My Idea was to combine all the words from the Part 1 solution and the Part 3 solution. Together they would form the answer to Part 4. ! + 3= 4, So I made my grid 25 boxes wide,because of the 4 parts to Kryptos and the 4 parts to the giant cross of America, made from the four States in the southwest, when looking at a map of America. I remembered that Mr Sanborn had created a Sculpture in New Mexico.

I started my grid with the words from the first solution, in the order they were written, leaving a open box between each letter of each and between each word from the 13 words of the solution of part one. I continued writing this pattern down 25 letters wide and 27 lines down. Then I added the words from Part 3 solution, starting back at the beginning or the top of the page, with the word B e t w e e n and added all of the rest of the letters from the words of the part 3 solution in the order they were written. I just thought it was neat finding the name FENN 5 times raising up to the right hand of my page, just like Part 4 of Kryptos does with Mr. Sanborns Sculpture. One of the name FENN, had a F before the word FFENN. I just thought it was interesting that two unsolved puzzles, or at least the name behind one of the puzzles in our Country could be found in Mr Sanborns Puzzle Kryptos. I just like solving puzzles and hope that they are put on with endings that are not harmful to anyone. I'm unable to physically search for the answers, so I try to help the [courriel] in other ways. Hope I have been helpful to someone out there.

William C. Papke

Hi Greg,

I read your e-book a while back (it's very good btw!) and noticed some overlap with my own research.

You included a visual of the main gearing mechanism of the Antikythera mechanism as well as a discussion of the approach taken by 'The Machinists' in cracking the mathematical puzzle at the heart of the story.  You have obviously mentioned Bletchley Park and Turing, but what aspects of your research to date led you to include the other angles mentioned previously?

The exposition of the metadata showing that Kryptos is both a functional and symbolic analogue to the Antikythera mechanism has been sitting in the files area since 2017 and is based on previous work published in 2013.  Nobody appeared to have taken any notice of it, so very interested to know more about your thoughts on this.

With regards the recent Sanborn studio and on site sculpture visit,  there were various clues that further convinced me that we are looking at a solar/lunar cycle calculator augmented by the Venus sun conjunction cycle.  The hand exhibit that looked like a relic from a lost civilization had 18 beads arranged around it in the form of a bracelet.  (I took this to be visually indicative of the Saros cycle.)

The reference to the book that Jim was reading whilst making the sculpture was also an interesting potential clue.  The book, 'Still Life with Woodpecker' is all about the true purpose of the moon!

Can you tell us something more about your method for how you arrived at the plaintext?

Many thanks,
Matt

s: Illusions: K1, the Memorial Garden and the Memorial Wall
t:
Without delving too much into details on the "Wondrous Patterns" golden bough key path I’ve been following in my pattern study of K4, I came up with some results after that particular key concept led me to the CIA Memorial Garden’s koi pond and waterfall area. Specifically, as K1 relates to the plaque that was placed there.

"In remembrance of those whose unheralded efforts served a grateful nation" vs
"Between subtle shading and the absence of light lies the nuance of iqlusion."

After noticing NCEOF in there, I wondered how much of the speech could anagram to K1. The answer was: a lot.

I came up with two sets of result after using an excel spreadsheet to mark off shared letters and studying the remainder. No particular order.

Plaque: DAVE RR RR RR FF OO MM alternatively DAVE FROM FROM

K1:  NINTH IS QUILL BBGC

Put those words together and you get something that means plenty in context of Book 9 of the Aeneid, but more to the point, ALSO means something on the Memorial Wall of Stars names. To the point:

In 1961, Thomas W Ray (smokejumper) and David W Bevan (paratrooper)  were killed and are honored on the wall. There’s 8 total, nine if you include a civilian casualty. The other names have similar correlation with BBGC.

Conclusion: This has some potential implications about the nature of K4 in regards to concealment of spies and spying devices among civilian population (fake airline) or natural environments (see the infamous robot catfish in the CIA museum that somewhat resembles a koi fish with their odd little whiskers. It may be that K4 is illusionary, some non-standard elements that make it appear to be something it is not – such as the difference between cipher and code, iirc. For example, it appears that the first 22-24 letters may actually be an advanced anagram involving a bough, brook and bulbs – aka the memorial garden.

James

Since there has been some interest in this topic, I just posted some photos of a custom-made Antikythera mechanism which was on display at a classic computer show. (by Bob Roswell)

Larry

That's a nice reproduction!  Did it also have a planetary dial on the back?  Interestingly the gearing of the planetary face is mostly conjecture due to how much of the mechanism was lost, but its an incredible piece of kit.  I've also seen a reconstruction using Lego and Hublot somehow managed to compress the whole thing down into a mechanism the size of a wrist watch!Perhaps my favourite rendition of the mechanism though has to be Kryptos itself!
Just to circle back for those that may be confused, Mark Brady derived Quincunx as a K1 keyword and Greg Materna featured an image of the Antikythera mechanisms famous quincunx gear housing in his recent book that has Kryptos as a fundamental thread of the story.
For my part, I have files in the personal files area that detail how the Saros and Metonic cycle can be calculated from the Sculpture design.  Since then I've found an analogue to the third planetary dial, which I'm currently writing up (sorry for the wait), but like everybody I'm still scrabbling around trying to get a handle of K4.
Only potential ray of light on the horizon at present is that I have something akin to the Rosetta Stone setup whereby I have three quantities, a cipher mask, a plain text and a mapped text.

For (D)OBKRUO this has a cipher mask of PUNYYCK, a plain text of GKRYPTO and a mapped text of ESTEEPL (or steeple?).

The reasoning behind the first D as a 98th letter will be explained in the next paper, but I believe that we're looking at an interleaved stepping pattern of 7 letters being read at each step.  The process required uses 16 rows.  Interestingly there were 16 steps that led into KV62.

Will hopefully get back to finishing my next paper sometime soon!
Matt

s: Kryptos K4 - ALAN TURING and next word
t:
Hi all,

little update about the approach to solving K4.

firstly - BLETCHLEY PARK seems to be ok. I`ve found out what was the problem with B. What is more the approach is even better now since it uses another part of the Kryptos Sculpture that I didn`t use before.

secondly I couldn`t find any word before/after ALAN TURING - it seems that I finally found one that fits perfectly. The problem was that this word was not in the basic dictionary I`ve used. In summary it seems that words BOMBE, ALAN and TURING are three consecutive words.

Hello to all members of this group and thanks for letting me be a part of it.

As requested, here is a short introduction post: My name is Malte and i'm living in the northern part of Germany (Bremen to be precise).

I studied media technologies and got into cryptology because of a seminar I did on classical and modern algorithms. We started with Caesar and went to somewhere between DES and RSA. As I was more fascinated by the analogue systems, I focused on those and read a few books on them and tried some exercises I found on the web.

This is where I also got in touch with Kryptos. I saw a documentation on the "most interesting" unsolved codes and had a look on Elonka's page afterwards. I then tried to solve K3 with pencil and paper and also had a deeper look on the possibilities to solve K1 and K2 that way.

Now i have all my attention on K4 and the secret behind the masking technique. I have an idea what it could be like that i will share with the group in a following post.

Feel free to contact me via email (you can also write in German if you want). I cannot promise to have a look in here every day, but since Kryptos and K4 are fascinating, I do not think that i will be to far away at any time.

Greetings to all members!

As already said in my introduction post, I'd like to share some theories on K4 with the group. Feel free to comment on all of those.

Theres a lot of information on K4 already, but I will try to focus on what I think are major parts and what I propose from there:

- Jim Sanborn often said that he is not good at math. That could be a lie, but I will take it as a clue that a mathematical calculated cipher like Hill is not used. Theres a really good article on tests that Craig Bauer did with K4 and the Hill ciphers on Klaus Schmeh's blog. It more or less shows that a Hill cipher is not the right direction.

- The artist told at the 2019 meeting (and maybe more often, but I have read that in the notes from this years meeting) that he did the encoding on the way getting the pertrified tree for the sculpture. I think that this is also important as it also points away from anything that is too complicated to be realised.

- K1-K3 (and also the arragement for the whole sculpture) was done with pencil and paper. I do not know if Sanborn had the chance to use a computer at that time, but I do not think that the encoding was done with anything else than pencil and paper (maybe that already has been confirmed by Jim Samborn but I have not read it anywhere).

- K4s masking technique does not have a logic. When I started focussing on K4, I always tried to attack the ciphertext with bruteforce algorithms on the computer. None of my tries gave me something valuable. So I thought what the problem could be for a computer when trying to find a solution. The answer is that the cipher should not to be logical.

So, at the end, I'd propose that K4 has two steps: One is the unlogical masking of language, the other one is transposition.
I'll show my try on K4 with a technique that proofed to bring up the clue words in the following text. As said, feel free to comment on these proposals.

Malte

I really hope that this method has not already been discussed, but I think I have not seen it anywhere before. I will now show how I think K4 is encoded and what might be the mysterious masking.

1. Visual Masking

I thought a lot about what Jim Sanborn might have been doing while driving along the road, thinking of a system to encrypt K4. As an artist, I believe he chose a visual way of encoding. There are a lot of possibilities for visual encoding, but here, we do not see anything visually changed when regarding the letters on Kryptos. But what if the letters themselves are changed. And to make it even harder, not all are changed. I will make an example with the place where I read BERLIN when revealing the masking:

Its starting at position 16 where the letters on Kryptos read: LIFBBW
How to get BERLIN now?
We take one B and cut off the lower part of the letter and replace it with the stroke we need for R
R --> B (could be like this on a palimpsest)
We then take the W and take away the left stroke, we get N
N --> W
Last, the F has a missing stroke for beeing an E
F --> E

We then have LIERBN or BERLIN, if you change the letter order (Transposition)

Another example is the CLOCK, that should also appear in plaintext. This word can be found too with this visual masking.

Its starting at position 42, the letters are QSSEK

1. Q becomes O just by removing the stroke
2. S can be cut at the middle and becomes C (not really good visible here, but if you look onto Sanborns Sheets you will see that the artists writing shows that its visually possible)
3. Remove two strokes from the E and get L

We have OCCLK or CLOCK

After these letters, ZZWA is following, removing the strokes from the Z's, it could be LLWA or WALL, which would fit cause Berlin had the WALL at the time Kryptos was created.The first two letters OB could be OD or DO in plaintext.

2. Transposition Step 1:

There also is a correspondance between the two examples when regarding the transposition of the letters in both words.

LIERBN --> BERLIN : 123456 --> 534126

OCCLK --> CLOCK : 12345 --> 34125

LLWA --> WALL : 1234 --> 3412

3. Transposition Step 2:

Now the only thing left to do is to rearrange the word order because they are at the wrong position. This could have been done by a matrix that consists of words other than letters. If you write them down, you can get the following. Note that I do not have completely deciphered everything so some letters are still ciphertext and that the words that are guessed plaintext could also be wrong.

OBK		YOUR		GO		SHOULD		BERLIN		FLRV
POOR		WAY		SSO	INTO		CLOCK		WALL
IT			OVER		THIN	END		NYPVTT		MZFPK
WGDKZ	X	ITS			DIGK	UHU		AUE			CAR

The X can be a Y or an X as stop symbol. I also tried to take K as a Y, but that did not proof to be a right way. In this test-matrix, the beginning of BERLIN is at Position 58, if you read the words by column now. As it depends on the other words so its possible that it starts at 64 when having deciphered everything.

As already said, I am not sure if this type of masking is the right way. What made me focus on it is the really fast and easy way to do it with pencil and paper and the big complexity the encryption has because not every letter is ciphertext.

Feel free to comment on all I posted.

Greetings from nothern Germany, Malte

It seems like you are saying that instead of NYPVTT (64-69) deciphering to BERLIN and MZFPK (70-74) to CLOCK, you have LIFBBW (16-21) and QSSEK (42-46) deciphering to BERLIN and CLOCK by a process of substitution and transposition which is different for different letters and groups. If you say "in one place I do this, and in another I do something completely different" that's arbitrary.

There's a good article out there called How to know that you haven't solved the Zodiac-340 cipher
which will help you out - what you're doing is disregarding half of Sanborn's clue (the location of the cribs) while using the other half (what the plaintext is). So it's a modified form of anagramming ("Warning sign #2").

In contrast, the other three parts of the Kryptos sculpture solution are consistent, easy to explain and code in your favourite programming language, and (dare I say it) use two very well known techniques from "American Cryptogram Association" puzzles. If you continue along the lines you've described you could up with anything, at the end, like saying your grandmother is the Zodiac killer.

best regards

Richard

---In [courriel],  wrote :

A really nice article and you're right, this try is all about anagramms and "finding" words that might fit in there and is not based on any well-known algorithm or anything.

I would not have posted it or taken it into account if there had not been the 2019-meeting where Sanborn has been asked about the positioning of the cribs. When reading Eloka's notes on Sanborn's answer, I understand that he has only said that K4 has 97 positions and that the plaintext BERLIN starts at position 64. Other sources from the past say that he has said something like N decodes to B and so on. I only took his latest answer which would make it possible that the ciphertext is at other positions than the plaintext.

But I also must say that this form of decryption is very "constructed"

While I don't have the same problems with anagramming that others do, and find certain elements of the spatial relationships/pattern formation between QSSEK/MZFPK and LIFBBW/BERLIN interesting, that seems to fall prey to an overinvolved level of complexity in deciphering the rest of K4. That's not to say it couldn't be a clue pointing to something else, because I believe there are quite a lot of them in the Kryptos ciphertext. To see that relationship, plot out a 4x24 grid for K4, with R on the final line. You'll find LIFBBW and NYPVTT fall on a diagonal strip similar to the tableau effect on the right side of the table. QSSEK and MZFPK, otoh, are in opposite positions on alternating lines.

    Personally, though, I like the idea because it reduces... on an artistic level... the homophonic substitution ciphers (what you seem to be describing here) and null ciphers (anagramming) to their absolute most rudimentary origins - sticks and leaves. Sticks for the shapes of letters, leaves for the oracles from whom anagramming is believed to have originated.

   Combining the three (sticks, leaves and organization) in an orderly fashion that can be replicated by others seems to be a herculean task.

This past week I came across some old notes of mine from year’s
back- before Sanborn revealed the clue: Clock.
I ask myself, what should we do with past results which do not fit into
the 1-to-1, CT-to-PT, criteria?  Rather
than just backing up this information and never looking at them again- I wanted
to share, if by any miracle- it might shed light on a possibility of 2-to-1
criteria.

Years ago I cribbed dragged all the known plain text for the
first 97 letters (63 in K1 and 34 in K2) against K4 (key=Kryptos), and which I’m
sure many of us have done before.  Without any luck, I began substituting
Kryptos with other key words.  One of
them was the alphabet keyword, “Thorn”.  Like the thorn of a rose.  I had a
hit.  The K4 cipher text NYPVTT equaled
NCLOCK when I dragged TPOSSI.  That seems great; however the Berlin clue was
already given and NYPVTT equals BERLIN, not NCLOCK.  So I just disregarded as a coincidence.

Today, as I watched Sanborn’s lecture video (everyone has
seen) as he was showing images of his matrices.
He emphasized the section of ‘underground’…”. So I decided to crib drag more than just 97 letters
of the decrypted text- I crib dragged most of K2 and found text at K4
characters ZFPKWG which resulted in PT: ABEAST (or A Beast).  I wouldn’t have thought too much into it
however, the crib dragging portion happen to be the letters UNDERG
(underground?).  Maybe this is the beginning of K4?

Now, I’m in a dilemma:  to stop focusing on past results and go with
the 1-to-1 approach (NYPVTT=BERLIN and MZFPK=CLOCK).  Or do I continue down (or up) the path of
perhaps a 2-to-1 approach (NYPVTT=BERLIN (and NCLOCK) and MZFPKWG=CLOCK_ _ (and _ABEAST)?

The numerical value of the K1 plain text is weighing down on my at this point (666).  Can you see anything?  A Beast.

I hope everyone is well,

Kind regards,

Nicholas C. LaMey

If you do a search through the archive here for "Tribute", people wrote it's a "tribute to [CIA] employees" (Doug Price, Sep 2017), "tribute to Native American origins" (Elonka, June 2003), "tribute to cryptography" (CNN, June 2005) ... there's a "tribute to Solaris" (de Boer, June 2014) ...

but amusingly, in over 20,000 messages, nobody's mentioned the name of the sculpture in the CIA files, which is "Tribute To Information". It's virtually disappeared off the net ... a newspapers.com or Factiva search will turn it up (Guardian 12 March 1991 "Art of Deception has CIA baffled", Martin Walker), there's one result in books.google.com plus one in normal google (Time magazine 18 March 1991 "The Spooks' Secret Sculpture Garden" and 24 June 2001 "Grapevine", both David Ellis). If Jew-Lee hadn't scanned the Cryptogram you'd have to join the ACA and trawl through back issues to find the speech ... if you even knew it was there ... which goes to show all the info about the sculpture will gradually fade away, and/or disappear behind paywalls. Better make sure your PDF files are searchable with text!

s: An Idea how to solve part 4 of Kryptos
t:
Hi, [courriel] ,

I was playing with some letters of the Kryptos puzzle.

I picked out all the 7 lettered words from the beginning word Between to Emerged.

So I stacked the words vertically with the word Between on the upper left hand corner, then the word Shading, then the word Absence and continued onto the word Seventy.

The first 11 words on the third row horizontally down from from the first word Between it spells out T A S T. I thought the A S T might be from the T I S A S T B A L L O O N. I believe this was the decipher from the Part 1 solution.

So I had seen that from the last letter Y in Langley to the last letter in Seventy it spells out Y E S S S Y

The next six words Degrees , Minutes, Seconds, Remains, Passage and Doorway almost spelled out Y E S S S Y , It was only one letter off Y E S S S S , when you start with the word Degrees with the s below the y of seventy or your writing the next 11 words from Degrees to Emerged up side down and back to the left hand side of your paper , for me.

Then I wondered if as a reflection as if a mirror looked into what might appear. The mirror might be from the reflection off of the pond at Kryptos.

So I switched around all of the letters that did not match where both seven lettered words meet in the middle when written 11 forward Between to Seventy
 and 11 backwards from Degrees to Emerged.

My new order for the top 11 words Between through Seventy were written down vertically as Between and then the word Shading written upside down or the letter g from shading now next to the B from Between then the word Absence starting with the A at the top then the word Flicker, then the word Details, written upside down with the S at the top. then the word Langley, with the L at the top, then the word Message with the M at the top, then the word Degrees with the D at the top, then the word Minutes with the M at the top,then the word Seconds with the S at the top and the word Seventy
with the S at the top.

Where both sets of the  11, 7 lettered words meet I came up with N S E R D Y E S S S Y. The 11, 7 lettered words on the bottom from left to right were

the words Unknown, Degrees, then the word Emerged written from the top with the letter E beneath the word Absence, then the rest of the words,

Chamber, Removed, Doorway, Passage, Remains, Seconds, Minutes, Totally all written upside down.

When I had finished this the letters T I S appeared on the same 3rd line down from the word Between.

Then I brought up the hole bottom row of the letters U D D C R D P R S M T and placed them on top of the letters B G A F S L M D M S S, so I could get the B A L or the next three letters of T I S A S T B A L   L O O N . I thought once you get the full T I S A S T B A L L O O N spelled out you would have the proper 3 letters  that lead you to the three words that you change  out seven times with the three seven lettered words Between, Shading,

Absence to unlock this code. Maybe it has 7 times 13 = 91 and the 6 letters left over from the 8th seven lettered word adds up to 97.

I hope this has helped someone with more Knowledge of these codes and ciphers from our [courriel] yahoogroups.com to solve this puzzle from Mr. James Sanborn and his beautiful piece of Art he named Kryptos.

William C. Papke

I'll add to this request:  Do we have any unambiguous statement from either JS or ES that the masking is a separate step, be it before or after 'encryption'?   The quote in my mind, attrib. to ES, is approximately "In the other sections you had access to the English language statistics, but [in the last section] you don't have access to those because I masked that".   (Incidentally, note the first person construction - and never worry about Jim being an "anamath" - the mathematical parts of this were taken care of by somebody who isn't  anamatth at all.)  E.g., if you add an apparently random string of  numbers (as lengthy as your plaintext) to a converted-to-numbers plaintext you have both encrypted and masked at once.

Jim has said you can't, so to speak, unravel this in reverse, you must first figure out what he did - presumably from clues in the sculpture.  If you knew the mask step & encryption step, assuming they are separate, it really wouldn't be important which was first..  You have two possibilities to try.

Example (using my own pet theories):  Encode your PT with a Vig. table keyed KRYPTOS and message key 'BERLINP", and convert to numerals.  Produce a long string of numbers (preferably prime so as to avoid inadvertent repetitions) such as the decimal part of 19/563.  Scramble this series, if you want to make it harder to crack, by taking the numbers from this original string in some particular order, say every 13th one, to form a derivative string which doesn't resemble any string known to the OEIS or anybody else.  Add the numbers from this derivative series, by singles or doubles, to your numerical encryption from the Vig. table.  Convert back to letters (using base 26 if you've used pairs rather singles).

If you haven't figured out the key to the Vig. table, the message key, the derivation of the masking string &/or complications of same, and so on, this is essentially impossible.  If you definitely do know those things, it's as easy for Eve as for Bob.   I'm not saying the example is necessarily how this has been done, but that if you can figure out what he did, it's no matter how hard it would be if you can't.  FWIW, JS says you can't do it until you understand his method.

For those who haven't followed my opinions on old posts:  We have one key clue, courtesy Scott Perry, by decrypting K4 with a message key of the first 11 letters of K1, EMUFPHZLRFA, on a Vig. table keyed with KRYPTOS.  "[T]hen transpose by counting every 38th letter starting at the location of the 77th letter."  Starting at the 64th letter of the result, there appears the series BERLINPEEKRRR (then gibberish).   I believe the final 3 Rs are allusions to Cyrillic YA and signify "back(ward), back(ward), back(ward)", giving KEE, and leaving BERLINP.  Whether the 'Kee' is to a Vig table, the message on a KRYPTOS Vig table, something else entirely,  is it BERLINP, BERLIN (Palimpsest), PNILREB, that we aren't told, but it's plain enough we're told it's a key in some way.

We have a number, 563, brought to our attention in various ways (details on request, or in my old posts here) which as a divisor of any integer will produce one of two possible decimal series of 281 digits each  (repeating infinitely, starting point in either series depending on the dividend).  These series seem likely candidates for an original series as above, for a mask.  Whether that is the case or not,  we are pretty clearly to do something with 563.

When we figure out what to do with what we've got, it won't really matter whether the egg came before the chicken or vice-versa - or whether the chicken ~is~ the egg.

Ed never answered the question about whether "masking" was performed before, after, or as an integral part of, the encryption.

All he really ever said was that in K1..K3 we could use knowledge of english language statistics to solve the encryption, and that K4 was more complicated and "removed the advantage" of knowing the statistics of the plaintext.

We ASSUMED there was a masking STEP, and asked whether he applied such step before/after the encryption.  He smiled, and merely said "that's an interesting question".  I interpreted his answer to mean, "Interesting that you guys assumed there was a processing STEP -- we never said that".

While there could be an explicit STEP, I wouldn't take his answer as confirming our assumption that a masking step is somehow applied.  If the encryption is sufficiently complex, having knowledge of the plaintext statistics doesn't help much, and serves to "mask" the statistics.

As an example, if you treat K1..K3 as training exercises for different cryptographic operations (substitution, transposition) and K4 combines these operations, we'd have a hard time figuring out what he did, even if we knew the underlying plaintext statistics.

I could be wrong, but I think the reason he "deferred" is that the question itself was flawed -- it presumed an explicit masking step and it may be that there is no such step.

I’d like to verify that he actually called out those letter positions...or was that someone’s interpretation of what he said. For instance if “CLOCK” started at 70 then that’s different than “it’s 70-74”. Plus he didn’t spell out C L O C K on paper as far as I can tell. I have my own theory...

Hi All – thought I’d share a little statistical coincidence that I found several months ago.

First, compare our plaintext crib (positions 64-74) with the implied key needed to convert

the ciphertext of K4 to that crib (Quagmire III, KRYPTOS mixed alphabet):

64 65 66 67 68 69 70 71 72 73 74

 B  E  R  L  I  N  C  L  O  C  K

 E  L  Y  O  I  E  C  B  A  Q  K

             *     *           *

Notice the correspondence between the key and PT in three positions. Now if the key was

completely uncorrelated with the PT, then on average you could expect a match between

a key letter and plaintext letter 3.8% of the time, and the odds of no matches out of 11

draws would be about 65% (i.e. the odds of at least one match are ~35%). But the odds of

3 or more letters matching is only 0.744%, or 1 in 134. Not a huge anomaly, but enough

that one might start to wonder if it’s a consequence of Ed’s masking technique.

And now for the real statistical oddity. Look at the plaintext characters of K3 at positions

64 to 74:

64 65 66 67 68 69 70 71 72 73 74

 P  R  N  G  A  T  I  H  N  R  A

             *     *           *

Note the locations of the vowels: they are identical to the positions in K4 where the key

equals the plaintext! Unfortunately, not all CT letters are possible with this system – only

every other letter of the Kryptos mixed alphabet (K, Y, T, S, B, D, F, H, J, M, Q, V and X).

The first five vowels of K3 correspond to the K4 CT letters O, U, O, O, L – none of which

can be produced by a system where CT = 2*PT. Still, this K3-K4 correspondence is

interesting.  --Rob

That's the way I remember the answer:
a.  consider the phrase "you had access to the English language statistics"  -- says that the Ciphertext was correlated to the plaintext, that the "statistics" were readily accessible/visible.
b.  then he says that "but [in the last section] you don't have access to those because I masked that".  Read this carefully -- you don't have access to the statistics because I masked that access.

We jumped all over his word "masked"  -- we assumed the object of the verb was the plaintext and/or ciphertext;  we assumed there was a masking step;  we made lots of assumptions based on how WE would do it, but he never said any such thing.

Knowing nothing about K4, my initial assumption was that K1..K3 formed an "agent training" exercise to demonstrate substitution and transposition.  That's why I thought Scott Perry was on the right track for a system that combined substitution & transposition: "We have one key clue, courtesy Scott Perry, by decrypting K4 with a message key of the first 11 letters of K1, EMUFPHZLRFA, on a Vig. table keyed with KRYPTOS.  "[T]hen transpose by counting every 38th letter starting at the location of the 77th letter."  Starting at the 64th letter of the result, there appears the series BERLINPEEKRRR (then gibberish)."

Note also we ASSUMED that transposition was ruled out by his comment that the 6 letters of ciphertext matches the 6 letters of BERLIN.  That assumption was based on how WE would likely do transposition.

There's another way:  instead of substituting in linear order (letter 1, followed by letter 2, etc) we can perform substitution in a skip order:  letter 1, followed by letter 1 + n,  followed by letter 1 + 2n, etc.  This is mathematically equivalent to three steps transpose, substitute 1-2-3..., and inverse transpose.  But it has the property that the PT and corresponding CT positions match, which is all that Ed really told us.

So if we follow Scott's formulation, substitute (Vig with key EMUFPHZLRFA) in the "transposed order" 1,1+38, 1+2*38, etc. we get to BERLIN.  Then something goes awry in the next substitutions such that CLOCK gets garbled.

We don't know the process he used, but it probably involves grids like he used in K1..K3.  His process for using the grids may combine substitution and transposition in one easy step.  Maybe he made a mistake somewhere which we need to correct for to fix the garble.

I find the fact that BERLIN is at 63 (counting from 0) which is 7 times 9;  and Scott's starting point is 11 times 7.  Could be coincidence, or could mean there's a grid with 7 letters and Jim just read one of the rows when he gave us the initial crib.

Bottom line I believe Scott's formulation is consistent with Ed's comment that "I did something to mask the statistics" and that there's no explicit masking "step".

I think we presented Ed with a unanswerable question "did you mask the plaintext or the ciphertext".  He couldn't confirm there was or was not a masking step, so no matter what answer he came up with it would convey information he was not willing to convey.  Hence he ducked, "that's an interesting question..." and moved on.

Looking at "how to find the key for kryptos" in instructables by Starlifter, and a few other resources, i feel that the k4 section is encrypted twice using probably both the vigenere cipher (as per k1 and k2) and transposition (k3).

So i started off with "kryptos" as the alphabet key in the vigenere cipher, and then using the cipher text looked for patterns or letters that would start spelling out the end solution.

After a couple of hours i had found (probably mentally forced) the first part of the message to read "wait the time and space". Happy with that i looked at my passphrase to see if i could find any patterns either within it or correlation between it and the ciphertext. Some hits some misses, but i thought worth a punt.

Not knowing what words/phrase might come in the next few letters i start inputting letters into my passphrase to see the outcomes. Turns out all it took was one letter to decipher the next few words. I tried repeating the passphrase again and it failed. Tried different spacing and all kinds of options, but all failed. I continued to try to solve the section after Berlin clock, and through trail and elimination found the words "brings our hope together".

Now i am left with a section of text between the solution i have found but stuck at a dead end. I would guess that the 2nd half of the passphrase repeats itself at some point, and that the two could be solved seperately.

Next guess it to find a pattern, repeat the 2nd part of my passphrase, then reverse engineer the entire passphrase to find another key that could prove what i have done is somewhat correct. Not taking into account any deliberate errors, may make this part more difficult.

With all due respect to ES, there's a lot of ways to work around his knowledgebase by incorporating material that is not part of his skillset, such as that of the arts, in this case literature. By not using any of the classical ciphers, and embedding secondary clues in the CIPHERTEXT (specifically, not the plaintext), then combining simple methods with an alien knowledgebase he can make an expert start from scratch in something that isn't a true cipher but more like a pile of masks.

All that said, I'm not sure a real hardcore cryptoanalyst would appreciate the.... inventiveness.

To point: Without any knowledge of Greek mythology/history and classic literature of Virgil, your average person is unlikely to know what The Sibyl and Aeneid  are or how it ties into the foundations of Christianity and a long series of past and present history..

K4 has a bunch of "Eye Clues" and this was the first discovery I've made that actually gives it context.

t:
Carl,I had to create some constraints for myself because of the number of iterations I have been through on this. I didn’t want to slip into any other substitutions that I had used previously.  I wanted the process to lead me where it was going to lead me.

As to the full BERLINCLOCK being in the position it was in, everything I have read about this indicates that the specific cipher letters, NYPVTTMZFPK, had direct substitutes as per your reference. Their location in the cipher identifies their position...side-by-side.  That is what the table I provided shows. The top row letters are directly replaced by those in the bottom row. Constraint #2 is consistent with frequency analysis methodology. When a letter is replaced anywhere in the cipher,  any other location for that letter is also replaced. You then look at the new configuration of the entire cipher text and see if there are any new word possibilities that have surfaced.

The quandary I am in now is that there are very few letters that can be changed after this without changing the BERLINCLOCK text due to further substitutions of those letters elsewhere in the cipher text.

Perhaps my constraints are unrealistic. I have been trying to adhere to frequency analysis methodology but obviously something else needs to occur to decipher the rest of K4. My question was to the team to see if there was another level of cryptology that should follow. I have read that some think there are two levels of encryption at work here - possibly a combination of routing transposition and a vigenere table. As it is, I am left with the BERLINCLOCK text where it is supposed to be (according to my understanding of Sanborn’s statements) and a bunch of undeciphered text.

Regards,
Scott Gressel

s: Kryptos: The Sibyl, the Pyramid’ s Apex and Novus Ordo Seclorum
t:
Re: The Sibyl, Cribs and Frequency Analysis

Because I brought up cribs earlier, I figured I should revisit that at least briefly and explain for newer members. If you’re aware of Vigenere cryptoanalysis, you know that in addition to frequency analysis as a cryptoanalytic attack, there is also the method referred to as a known-plain text attack, "crib" or "kiss". Repeated sequences of letters are suspect and help solve in Vignere. Given that Kryptos K1-K2 were already solved long ago, it doesn’t get a lot of attention, but these cribs exist in K1 and K2 as well.

K1 – VJYQT = NCEOF
K2 – GWHKK = SIBLE
K2 – DQM = THE

I theorized that because Jim expected these two sections of Kryptos to be solved quickly, it might be that these cryptoanalytic patterns might be meant to provide clues, with more simple mechanisms than a full blown cipher.

This is what was intended when I brought up the SIBLE/SIBYL cribs in K1 and K2.

James

The final part is obviously the, you know, the apex of the pyramid there" may contain a completely overlooked clue if taken literally.  This figure of 80% is interesting.  This next statement will immediately divide the community here, so buckle in as we're possibly about to split into two camps.
The evidence I have points to K4 being interleaved.  The opening statement about the possible decryption above is formed from 3 blocks that read 6 letters at a time.
OBKRUO
XOGHUL *
BSOLIF

Blocks 1 and 3 were 'encrypted' using the row idendification scheme already outlined in previous papers that shows acrostics of NORTH and SOUTH.  Here's the kicker.  That second block was read literally from the cipher text using the last 7 letters of K4 AUEKCAR.

A U EKC A R
UR corresponds to the spelling mistakes in the acrostic/telestich that cuts across the second block of six, which to remind you are SO(C)TH and NO(T)TH.
AA gives the start and end letters for positions with in the first two rows.
EKC is the alignment of all three rows.

I was hoping to generate some discussion off the back of this thread for or against the reasoning used, so I'll dig in a little deeper to see if I can kick start it.

'The Machine' would appear to be a secondary layer from what I gather at this stage.  As you see from the previous papers there is a coordinate system in the top left that doubles up as a drive wheel in a mechanical system that mimics the axial rotation of the earth.  A nod towards this may appear in the K3 string: 'REACH IN THE UPPER LEFT HAND CORNER'.  It was only in the last few months I noticed that this re-arranges nicely to (R)ACHINE IN THE UPPER LEFT HAND CORNER.

Putting the Antikythera work aside for a moment and concentrating on K4, if we isolate the calendar section in the stego scheme then you are left with 14 rows of 19 characters in the top and bottom panels giving 266 blocks a piece.  I'm assuming that six blocks are always being read off, so that really gives you 260 blocks for the top and bottom panels.  I'm now of the opinion that these are the WESTERLY and EASTERLY elongations of VENUS as it makes it way round the sun.  This has a basis in Mayan astronomy, but I'll leave that for the long form paper, the key thing is that it gives us 4 potential modes. 2 for West and 2 for East.  I outlined the first westerly mode yesterday, so now I'll make a conjecture about the 2nd westerly mode, which you'll find attached in my personal files.  It relies on a Q being read as on O, but otherwise it would look like a potential scheme for the 2nd Westerly mode would be 'decrypting' and reading in the upwards direction with 'no interleaving'.  You'll notice this time that the row correlation occurs when there is 3 letter match in both the plaintext and the cipher text.
Running an algorithm to identify such row matches turns up too many possibilities, so there must be a secondary system in place to resolve the ambiguity as shown in the first westerly mode if this is indeed the solver for BERLIN CLOCK.

At the heart of this is WW, i.e. the two lines stacked above each other in rows 14 and 15 that read WESTIDBYROWS and
WLYTHEREMAINS.

These transform to give
WESTXLAYERTWO and
WESTHLAYERMIN

I haven't played with anagrams of EAST yet as this research has only come about in the last half year or so, but I think its worth exploring further.  I'm happy that the Antikythera work stands on its own merits as being self consistent, so please feel free to join me on this particular thread as the research is in a much earlier stage.

in rows of 5 letters. Corresponding to the five letters of DYAHR.

R     YA

Y.  Therefore we can identify the columns for Y, A and H. (Columns 4, 5
and 2 respectively)  Assume D and R are a unit with their respective H and
YA respectively.

Perform  columnar transposition
(34521) resulting in the YAR in row 15 and D H in row 20.

 Move DH up to Row 15 (which is the row in the sculpture

s: The Blinking Eye - The Sibyl - EYOIE CBAKQ
t:
Note for Newer Members: The standard form of Kryptos you see on screen/paper, even that used by the CIA, is technically wrong. The Kryptos Tableau does not sit next to a regular Vigenere Tableau, but a *reversed* Tableau. You have to look at a picture of Kryptos to pick this up. What this means is that the outlying “L” is at the center of Kryptos, not the outer-rim, and the columnar “rays” point the opposite way. Relevance addressed at end of post.

Recurring theme: The Blinking Eye

 “HOT AIR ESCAPING FROM THE CHAMBER CAUSED THE FLAME TO FLICKER”
See also:  K3 plaintext

BERLIN CLOCK – Speculated to be Mengenlehreuhr, a unique clock that tells the time by rectangles of light, while a light at the top blinks on and off, measuring the seconds.
See also: K4 plaintext

The SIBYL – Braziers of burning coal used for light and heat, notably an underground chamber associated with the oracular sibyl’s contemporary, the Oracle of Delphi, eyes that see the future..
See also: DYAHR = EBLIS and cryptoanalytic attacks = SIBLE

DYAHR – The illusionary Hydra that guards Tartarus in The Aeneid
See also: K3 ciphertext

HYDRA – A 2009 Jim Sanborn exhibit that shows the illusionary light effect of two beams of light crossed through a block of dry ice.
See also: Sanborn resume for video of exhibit

Hero & Leander – The Greek myth reference in the Sibyl Acrostic encircling the far-rows of a flattened Kryptos plaintext.  In Ovid’s Heroides, the doomed Leander swimming across a storm-tossed channel to meet his lady-love Hero at the Maiden’s Tower. As he swims, he sees the flame of the Tower, appearing to flicker because of the waves.
See also: HROHNL in K3 ciphertext

World Wonder Pharos Lighthouse – One of the earliest known lighthouses, using flame and brass mirror as their guiding light, no doubt flickering, and only visible from the proper angle.
See also SLLSLLNOHSNOS in K3 CT..  SLL SLL = WW NOHS NOS

The Great Seal of the USA – Incorporated into many officers of leadership in US government, it has not only a front/obverse, but a back/reverse. On the back is a visual usually seen on the back of a dollar bill – the “Eye” on the Pyramid, encircled by the NOVUS ORDO SECLORUM and associated with The Sibyl. The eye itself radiates light, as does the shield of 13 stars on the front. No eye, merely a field of light stars on blue in a similar circle of rays. Night and day.

Tutankhamun’s Mask – One of the first items found by Howard Karter (again, K3) was this, and the eyes have a similar representation. Without getting deep into symbology, one is day, and the other is night. Darkness and light.
See also: K3 plaintext
ELYOIE CBAKQ – A phonemic puzzle?
See also:  BERLIN CLOCK vigenere discussion and Elonka’s CIA pictures

EL = L, the center of Kryptos
Y = Y formation created by the natural rays of a vigenere tableau
O = OH, subtle circular shading on the front of Kryptos, Image 1103, Kryptos folder
IE = Eye, the semi-circular shadow around the OH on the same image
CBAQK = See Back

On the front of Kryptos you see the illuminated letters. On the back, unlit letters. The eye opens and closes, blinking based on movement from position to position.
See also: K1-K2 wrap in plaintext. IQLUSIONIT = “…Eye Clues. Eye On It…”

We spent quite a bit of time asking Jim about the correlation between

the plaintext BERLIN and the ciphertext such as NYPVTT. Specifically, we

were trying to find out if there was a 1:1 relationship from NYPVTT to

BERLIN, or there was some other step, the masking technique. Jim was

confused when we mentioned masking technique, evidently it's something

that Ed said that Jim didn't understand. Jim said that yes the

ciphertext and plaintext were connected, but when I tried to explain

what exactly we were asking, like that in K1 EMUFPH is exactly BETWEE,

but in K3 ENDYAH does not map exactly to SLOWLY, Jim backed off and said

he would only commit to the fact that K4 is exactly 97 characters long,

and that BERLIN is plaintext that starts at exactly the 64th character,

but he wouldn't go further than that.

Jim can respond in three possible ways:

1. Jim confirms a similar pattern like K3 - there is transposition involved (step 1 for the key and/or ciphertext) and then some form of substitution (64th position - step 2)

2. Jim flat out denies some sort of mapping (i.e. no transposition) - some elaborate key & cipher would be required to substitute all 97 characters. Again, there would be some hint given (i.e. a third deciphering tableau on the panels) for pure substitution

3. Jim declines to answer - Jim is aware that transposition IS used (on the key and/or ciphertext) and is attempting to circumvent the inquiry.

K1-K3 required the assembly of the key through a certain algorithm to obtain the plaintext. K1 & K2 can be "paper and pencil" solved by using the upper and lower half of the tableau through stenographic clues. K3 had multiple keys available to manipulate the ciphertext.

Perhaps Jim encoded K4 merely by concealment (four -> PHOAR), substitution, then transposition, then the decryption would involve some form of transposition, decrypt substitution, and then some human trial and error for concealment.

s: "The Sun is God" : Turning the K/E/Y
t:
While I’ve been examining the Kryptos text itself, I’ve also been checking for clues in the arts that might attached themselves to the various themes I’ve uncovered in the plain and cipher texts. I was a little startled when I came across a painter named JMW Turner and had immediate hits  with an artist named JMW Turner not just for the Sibyl, but for Carnaervon and the Hero/Leander myth. Extended study shows that many of the paintings appear to run parallel, even a drawing of a cradle/crib that has the word FEET at the bottom, in parallel to the PRNG/TEEF text on Kryptos. Basically not just a few clues, but most if not all of them.

This artist is known for a few things, first being a near contemporary of the same era as the artist Frederic Leighton from the Acrostic, dipolar as a Modern Artist to Leighton’s Academic. More importantly, his entire painting style focuses on a few recurring elements from Kryptos … a horizon (abscissa), watercolor wet on dry (palimpsest/pentimento and the diffusion of rays of light from the sun (0362514 ray coordinates) His entire style is in fact obsessive in focus on a few elements, always including the play of light and darkness, with a preference for storm tossed waves and lighthouses. This obsession included an unfortunate habit of sun-gazing, the final words “The Sun is God”, and the title “Painter of Light”.

The last bit clicks with the cryptoanalytic clues – NCEOF SIBLE IGHT (Inks (or In Sea) of Visible Light when phonemically read.

  I chose five paintings to illustrate the point, but the huge body of work has more.

THE PARTING OF HERO AND LEANDER – An alternative perspective of Hero standing with a lantern on the Sestos shore for Leander’s across storm tossed waters to inevitable doom. The painting includes rays of light similar in striping to Tut’s headdress, an inverted “T” of light runs perpendicular to and along the shore, while a ray of light beams down in an eye-shaped cloud cover.
See: “I QLU” discussion, T IS HROHNL OVID, Sibyl Acrostic and K3/K4 crib text recurrence, Novum Ordo discussion

THE BAY OF BAIE, APOLLO AND THE SIBYL- The myth of Apollo in which the Sibyl fails a wish for eternal life and becomes something like an hourglass, or its predecessor the clepsydra Lotus Chalice, a first item found in Tuts Tomb.
See: Sanborn hourglass quote, K4 plaintext and extensive sun godâ€™s eye speculation.

CAERNARVON CASTLE - Lord Carnaervon and daughter Evelyn accompanied Carter at Tut’s tomb, noted to ask Carter what he sees by the light into the hole in the tomb.
See: K3 plaintext

BELL ROCK LIGHTHOUSE
B E l l   R o c k  L I g h t h o u s e
See: K4 plaintext BERLIN CLOCK, T IS HROHNL correlations of Hero and Leander’s Lighthouse and the World Wonder Pharos lighthouse.

Conclusion:  So how does it all fit together? The K/E/Y chart of +6/-6 text appears to show a pair of straight diagonal coordinates on line 1 and line 2, while the remaining two lines indicate a possible wave-like pattern based on the K3 coordinates. The Bell Rock clue may also hold some insight to this.

~ James

Hi Elonka,

Would it be possible for someone to ask Ed Scheidt the following questions for this year's dinner?

"If Jim released the CLOCK (2014) clue before BERLIN (2010) would there be a difference in the approach for K4?"
A: Yes - honest answer

B: No - lying

C: Defer to Jim - expected answer (see explanation below)

Explanation - Jim intended to release the hints in the order of BERLIN, then CLOCK because BERLIN provides vital clues on the approach, and CLOCK narrows down the possibilities when cribbing the solution. With the BERLIN clue only, I can hypothesize the decryption steps being transposition first, then substitution + concealment where K4 itself is the public key in an asymmetrical style cipher. CLOCK does not unequivocally provide the same level of hints to the decryption as BERLIN.

"In relation to the pencil and paper solution for K1 & K2, why do you think the K1 & K2 stenographic clues on the tableau side were missed?"
A: Don't know - Ed did not contribute the stenographic clues.

B: Mindset of cryptoanalysts - too much reliance on computers and trying all known ciphers

C: Other

D: Defer to Jim - expected answer (see explanation below)
Explanation - The stenographic clues in K1 & K2 reveal the cipher (Quagmire III substitution) and the size of the tableau. By using the symmetry of the cipher and the English language, the ciphertext can be run through the "shifts" for the pencil and paper solution. For K4, there are possible stenographic elements that have yet to be identified and may be essential to approaching K4. Ed's non-verbal response is more important.

"Yes or No: Did Jim intend to have a temporal element embedded within the Kryptos installation"

A: Yes - honest answer

B: No - would be lying

C: Defer to Jim - expected answer (see explanation below)

Explanation - K1, K2, K3 progresses through time in relation to significant American historical events that utilized cryptography. K4 is likely a continuance of the timeline and some inferences can also be made to eliminate many known substitution ciphers for K4. The transposition component might be embedded through stenographic means similar to K3.

Thanks!

P.S. In reference to your Kryptos PowerPoint slides, when Jim refers to one of the Kryptos pictures being ugly, Jim means that the dispersed light makes the sculpture dull and unflattering. The dispersed cloudy day soft lighting does not bring out the "serpentine S" structure through light and shadows. Jim is simply wishing his work is shown in the best possible light for aesthetic purposes.

My best results have been using a keylength of 97 and the BERLINCLOCK crib. I have successfully decoded K1 & K2 using a paper and pencil method, but have yet to recover the original keys for K3. The possible approach to K4 was assessed separately on an artistic level of Mr. Sanborn, and investigation into Mr. Scheidt's Moscow Billboard conjecture, both yielding very similar results on the approach.

I believe the primary setback of the groups' decryption of K4 lies in the success of Mr. Scheidt and Mr. Sanborn's leverage of "argumentum ad antiquitatem" (appeal to common practice). That is, we are trying to force K4 into a "known" ciphers with "known" decryption techniques, which is exactly the intention of Mr. Sanborn and Mr. Scheidt. A different approach might be to view K4 as first principles.

Fundamentally the classical (analog) ciphers utilize transposition(s) and/or substitution(s) to either change the position (same character), or character (same position). Mr. Scheidt's Moscow Billboard conjecture is simply a cryptic way to asking us to fundamentally evaluate classical ciphers (transposition/substitution) as well as the key/tableau delivery when both parties have all the information on a billboard. By evaluating the problem, we can determine the minimum number of encryption steps and keys so that the billboard is relatively secure. Once that is done, we can begin to understand when the masking layer is applied (on the ciphertext, plaintext, or intermediary) and FINALLY attempt the K4 decryption once we have determined the approach!

We shall see what happens when Mr. Sanborn releases his final clue this year!

Hi Luke: yep, it's been tried. Arguing against such a solution is that Jim Sanborn (at least initially) strongly implied
that NYPVTTMZFPK decoded letter-for-letter, 1-to-1 to BERLINCLOCK. Now I gather in a subsequent interview
there is some doubt that he understood (or fully appreciated) the question asked, and that all that he was
really willing to say was that "BERLINCLOCK" is the solution to positions 64-74 in the decoded text.

Even if he WAS willing to state for the record that N decodes to B, Y decodes to E, P decodes to R, etc., it
would still leave open the possibility that the keyword has been transposed or scrambled, which would
foil a computer dictionary attack. Still, simply combining transposition and substitution doesn't seem to
address Ed Scheidt's remarks about a "masking" step -- a step that seems to be a one-off system since I
believe he said something like it was "unknown by anyone on the planet," and that you would have to
solve that masking step first in order to be left with a classical cryptanalysis problem like that found in
K1-K3.

For such a multi-stage system to be "fair" and legitimately solvable, there would have to be some clue
(perhaps in the structure/layout of the sculpture itself) to steer us in the right direction. It can't be
something outside the serpentine sculpture (such as the stones with Morse Code or other elements
on the CIA grounds) because he has indicated that the table-top version of Kryptos has everything we
need. That doesn't leave a lot of extraneous elements to work with. Like many others, for years I focused
on possible systems hinted at by the raised YAR letters since they didn't seem to be unambiguously helpful
in solving any of the prior sections. But I believe Jim has (somewhat recently?) shared that those oddly
kerned letters in ENDYAHRO... have nothing to do with solving K4. That turned off a lot of analysts, which
probably partly explains the precipitous drop in postings to this group.  --Rob

Hi, I’ve been a lurker on the group for many years and I occasionally tinker with Kryptos. I thought I’d throw in a couple of ideas that I’ve been toying with. They haven’t led to anything for me but perhaps they could suggest further investigations.

1.    Combinatoric masking of the plaintext
Suggested by the Mengenlehreuhr (Berlin clock), I wondered if some modular arithmetic could provide a masking scheme which would be fairly simple to accomplish for a pen and paper encoder.

If you take a few numbers as a key, (e.g. 4, 5, 7 in the example below), you can create a sequence which could serve as a mask.

The sequence a = a(0), a(1), a(2),…  where a(n) is the sum of n modulo each of the numbers in your key (e.g. a(12)  =  12 mod(4) + 12 mod(5) + 12 mod(7) = 0+2+5 = 7). Elements of this sequence can then be added to the numerical values of the plaintext letters (a=0, b=1, etc.), to shift them.
n          …      12    13    14    15    16    17    18    19    20    …
4 mod(n)        0    1     2     3     0     1     2     3     0
5 mod(n)        2    3     4     0     1     2     3     4     5
7 mod(n)        5    6     0     1     2     3     4     5     6
a(n)                7    10     6     4     3     6     9    12    11
Plaintext        w    h     o     g     o     e     s     t     h
Ciphertext    d    r     u     k     r     k     b     f     s

Any sequence of this form would have some regularity, so I doubt this would ever serve as a code on its own, but when used in addition to a further coding step, it could just add enough extra obfuscation to throw off attempted decryption.

The numbers used could indicate a date and time or some other relevant detail.

2.    Possible book key
Here’s the other thing I’ve been looking at. This one is a long shot.

I’ve been looking at some stories by H. P. Lovecraft as possible sources for a book key. Particularly a paragraph from the (not very good) short story “The Lurking Fear”.
“On the tempest-racked night of November 8, 1921, with a lantern which cast charnel shadows, I stood digging alone and idiotically in the grave of Jan Martense. I had begun to dig in the afternoon, because a thunderstorm was brewing, and now that it was dark and the storm had burst above the maniacally thick foliage I was glad.”

Here’s my reasoning of why this might be a candidate:
It links to K3 because it was written in November 1922, about the same time Howard Carter was excavating Tutankhamun’s tomb.
The H in H. P. Lovecraft stands for Howard.
“Between subtle shading and the absence of light” could refer to the text between “shadow” and “dark” in the text.
The date in this paragraph can provide numbers for my combinatoric masking – 8, 11, 19, 21 – or some other use.
November seems to be significant to Kryptos. It was the month it was dedicated and the month each of the clues was given, and Jim Sanborn’s birthday is in November.
The story (not alone in HPL’s works) involves digging and discovering secrets.

Contraindications: It’s not very “on-message” for a piece of commissioned art. The CIA don’t really want to own a work saying “delving too deep leads to horror and madness”.

I’m sure thousands of other books and stories could have just as strong a set of connections to K3 (or other parts of Kryptos) as this one, though, including another HPL short story; “The Statement of Randolph Carter” (published 1920). That’s about a guy named Carter helping to break into an ancient tomb. Like Howard Carter speaking to Carnarvon, the guy entering the tomb did report back a little of what he saw to his companion. The program found three dozen cases of matching 8 out of 11 letters. Since this approach
doesn't utilize a "masking step," I consider it a dead-end.

There are an infinite # of masking ideas, so the only ones worth trying must somehow have
a connection to the sculpture. And it (probably?) can't be based on the plaintext of K1-K3
since Jim at one time said that solving K4 did not require solving the earlier sections. One
thing that stands out about K4 (as many have noted over the years) is the 31 characters
per line -- the highest number that can be represented in 5 bits (11111). Classical
cryptography problems usually provide the ciphertext in groups of 5 for easy legibility.
And while the raised YAR letters in K3 apparently have nothing to do with solving K4,
the 5-letter group DYAHR is offset from the preceding and following letters (and of
course anagrams to HARDY or, more thematically relevant, HYDRA -- given KRYPTOS
is Greek and the sculpture is shaped like a letter-S snake when viewed from above.)
So on my short list of masking ideas would be those that work on five letters at a
time.  --Rob
