s: Chaocipher encryption scheme - Progress, Candidate CT/PT alphabets
t:
Hi all,

Thought to start this thread to track the potential and/or dismissal of the Chaocipher encryption scheme used for K4 by Jim Sanborn.

So far the reverse engineering of  John F. Byrne's Chaocipher has hit no major road-block - I imagine that if Chaocipher is the wrong choice, it will break along the way when trying  potential CT/PT alphabets candidates.

I made some recent enhancements to get the process down from thousands of year to 175 days, and the latest, 20-30 days for producing the full NYPVTT/BERLIN CT/PT alphabets. Some  more time to go yet...

Progress Stats
-----------------
At cycle 1052 or 12650 we had 10,104 candidate alphabets to produce BERLIN. This then reduced (or increased) as per below:

7,989 —> BERLINC
6,193 —> BERLINCL
4,140 —> BERLINCLO
4,032 —> BERLINCLOC
2,754 —> BERLINCLOCK
12,168 —> ?BERLINCLOCK (many more successful combos due to the '?' wildcard)
zero! —> ??BERLINCLOCK (need to double check

Method
---------

Due to the permute process in the Chaocipher, we have to walk through many combinations of CT/PT alphabets - the total comes out as 1,935,632,160,000 combos

Create candidate CT alphabets - NYPVT(T)
-------------------------------------------------
* Loop through all possible arrangements of 4 characters into a 25 character array e.g. 0000000000000000000001111 — 16250 combinations
* We create a 26 character array from the above with the letter ’N’ pegged into the first position e.g. ’N’….
* Fill the above 25-char patterns with all possible non-duplicated arrangements of YPVT(T) - the second ’T’ is already included - 24 combinations
* Use the resulting 26-character array as a candidate CT alphabet

Combinations, nCr = 25!/(4! × (25 - 4)!) = 12,650 * 24 = 303,600

Create candidate PT alphabets - BERLIN
-----------------------------------------------
* Loop through all possible arrangements of 5 characters into a 25 character array e.g. 0000000000000000000011111 — 53130 combinations
* We create a 26 character array from the above with the letter ’B’ pegged into the first position e.g. ’B’….
* Fill the above 25-char patterns with all possible non-duplicated arrangements of ERLIN - 120 combinations
* Use the resulting 26-character array as a candidate PT alphabet

Combinations, nCr = 25!/(5! × (25 - 5)!) = 53,130 * 120 = 63,75,600

Discover Candidate CT/PT alphabets that produce BERLINCLOCK
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
* Fill in the above CT/PT candidates with known CT/PT pairs to discover potential BERLINCLOCK solutions
* This involves just trial-and-error by inserting known CT/PT pairs into the alphabet and testing the solutions

Discover Potential Decoded K4 Solutions
-----------------------------------------------
* We run the Chaocipher algorithm forwards using the potential CT/PT alphabets to see what potential outcomes there are
* Of particular interest are the outcomes that suggest three letters after BERLINCLOCK that suggest a good place for the word ”WAS” e.g. "... the Berlin Clock was ..."
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK......C.....R..........
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK......K............B...
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK......N................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK....I.K................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK....K.I............L...
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK....K.O............L...
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK....O.E.....N..........
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...B..O................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...E..N................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...E..O................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...I..N................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...LE.L............C...
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...N..I............B...
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...N..R................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...NE.I.....R..........
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...R..E................
    * Decoded: BERLINCLOCK...R..N............R...

Discover Potential CT/PT Alphabets Preceding BERLINCLOCK
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

This is by far the hardest bit I’d found however this does work:
* firstly, we are trying to find candidate CT/PT alphabets for BNYPVTTMZFPK —> ?BERLINCLOCK
* start with the CT/PT alphabets at ’N’,… & ‘B’,…
* permute backwards with ’N’ & ‘B’ at the zenith
* add place holders for the first unknown CT/PT pairs (ct=‘B’,pt=‘?’) by cycling all available free space combos of CT and then likewise cycling through all PT free space combos by inserting a  '?' in the hole AND also use the known PT characters as-is
* run the Chaocipher forwards and only those CT/PT alphabets that still produce ?BERLINCLOCK (where the '?' is the placeholder character or a known PT) are kept for further work

What was curious here is that the “?” char wasn’t part of any solutions - these are the only results remembering only 1/13th had been crunched so far...
BBERLINCLOCK
CBERLINCLOCK
EBERLINCLOCK
IBERLINCLOCK
KBERLINCLOCK
LBERLINCLOCK
NBERLINCLOCK
OBERLINCLOCK
RBERLINCLOCK

A sample Chaocipher CT/PT alphabet
-------------------------------------------
 The lower-case chars below are identifying place holders and can be ignored

ct=['B', '.', 'N', '.', '.', '.', '.', '.', 'Z', '.', 'M', '.', '.', '.', '.', '.', 'P', '.', '.', 'T', 'F', 'K', '.', 'V', 'Y', '.']
pt=['E', 'L', 'B', 'i', 'C', 'O', 'K', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h', 'j', 'k', 'l', 'm', 'R', 'n', 'o', 'p', 'q', 'I', 'N']

Now for FBNYPVTTMZFPK —> ??BERLINCLOCK
---------------------------------------------------------
Here is where we expect stuff to break if Chaocipher is not the method used because we’ve now got a bunch of CT/PT letters filled and now a known CT to trial-and-error with:
* start with all of the preceding the CT/PT alphabets at ’B’,… & ‘?’,… or ’B’,… & ‘E’,… etc
* permute backwards with ’B’ & ‘?’ or ’B’,… & ‘E’,… etc at the zenith
* add place holders for the first unknown CT/PT pairs (ct=‘F’,pt=‘?’) by cycling all available free space combos of CT and then likewise cycling through all PT free space combos by inserting a '?' in the hole AND also use the known PT characters as-is
* run the Choacipher forwards and only CT/PT alphabets that still produce ??BERLINCLOCK (where the ‘?’ is the placeholder character or a known PT) are kept for further work

As can be seen in the PROGRESS STATS above, we've now down to ZERO potential CT/PT alphabets to that can be successfully used to encipher FBNYPVTTMZFPK —> ??BERLINCLOCK. The caveat here is that all of the potential starting NYPVTT/BERLIN CT/PT alphabets are yet to be found...

If Chaocipher was not the technique used, then we will know when there are no potential CT/PT alphabets when working backwards so that we can start at OBKR and work all the way through to produce EASTNORTHEAST & BERLINCLOCK.

If Chaocipher IS the method used, then all good - we should have a few nice candidates *** Hopefully One! :) *** that decodes K4...

There is also the chance that the run backwards will exponentially explode with potential CT/PT pairs, if so I'll report that as well...

There is also the chance my 6 year old Mac may blow up first :P The fan has definitely started rattling a bit LOL

Cheers, Mike

Description:

x24 Array of K1-K3 coupled with MEMO Array in K4

K4 as a cryptogram - A depiction of alignments that match up between K4 and the K1-K3 plaintext, not limited to BERLIN.

Cryptograms vs Ciphers in K4 & Potential K4 Method

I believe that the reason K4 has managed to fly under the radar so long is because it is based on a system of cryptograms rather than ciphers – that is a series of word puzzles that contain ciphers, rather than a singular cipher.

There will be a file in JN’s Folder, Personal Files illustrating the alignments.

Following clues, x24 ARRAY appears to be a natural result, and while the series of cryptograms involved might be compared to Playfair in methodology, they’re really nothing alike.
An array being a simple arrangement of rows and columns
The system:
1. Arrange the plaintext of K1-K3 in rows of 24, flattened, and leave the question marks in. The final line will NOT be flush with the right.
2. Arrange the ciphertext of K4 in a MEMO array – that is two characters, followed by nine rows of 10 characters, followed by 5 charactrs. Left-side justified.

The results:
1.    NYPVT aligns perfectly with NY-OUS (PVT Caesar shift)on a diagonal course.
2.    BER and LIN form an equal sign in Column 12 on a vertical course to NYOUS..
3.    Interestingly, 12 is also the Caesar shift of B to N….
4.    SEK aligns with HBP – the two are a Caesar Shift of each other.
5.    EKCA aligns with UBRT – also a mixed Caesar shift.
6.    NYP aligns with LWN – again, a Caesar shift.

Also notable, but not shown is that the end of NORTH in K2 aligns with the beginning of NORTH in K4.

There’s clearly something going on here that is more Cryptogram than Cipher.

I must emphasize that this new finding remains at the level of a striking *statistical* correlation between my proposed method, as I have shared in several posts in this group and in the Techniques subgroup, and the possible beginning of the K4 plaintext message "BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES EASTNORTHEAST", which strikes me as a rather plausible and natural 21-letter phrase to appear before EASTNORTHEAST in the message.

It strikes me as plausible and natural for several reasons: It is exactly the right number of letters, without any artificial misspellings, filler letters, or omitted letters. Seventy (70) degrees is indeed extremely close to true Eastnortheast, which is 67.5 degrees east of true north or magnetic north. Even if one were to use such precise nearby compass directions as "East by North" (78.75 degrees) and "Northeast by East" (56.25 degrees), seventy degrees would still be closer to Eastnortheast than to either of these other nearby precise compass directions. Finally, "bearing" is both a natural colloquial term and a precise technical term relating to compass navigation: "In navigation, bearing is the horizontal angle between the direction of an object and another object, or between it and that of true north. Absolute bearing refers to the angle between the magnetic north (magnetic bearing) or true north (true bearing) and an object. For example, an object to the East would have an absolute bearing of 90 degrees." (<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bearing_(angle)>)

My proposed method can quickly and efficiently reject the vast majority of possible crib words and phrases as potential K4 plaintext in particular places in the message, as most of them require random row and column shifts within the DYAHR-keyed Polybius square in order for the final Playfair encryption step to produce the K4 ciphertext. Random row and column shifts have roughly equal amounts of the shift values 0,1,2,3,4 within the 5x5 square, whereas in my method a 4 shift is rare (7.5-8% of shifts) and a 3 shift is also less frequent (12-15% of shifts). According to my most updated prior analysis, a 2 shift should be by far the most frequent (34% of all shifts) for the 1st half of K4, as it is for EASTNORTHEAST. I have rejected very many possible crib words and phrases for the K4 plaintext that I would otherwise consider plausible, because the required row and column shifts to make them fit my method do not correspond with statistically plausible frequencies of such shifts according to my method. For example, I had been quite fond of the idea that the Berlin street name KURFURSTENDAMM or KURFUERSTENDAMM could appear in the K4 plaintext, but the required row and column shift statistics have not backed up this idea according to my proposed method. Likewise, such statistics have shown no support for such possible K4 plaintext words/phrases as BRANDENBURG GATE, CHECKPOINT (as in CHARLIE), or POTSDAMER PLATZ at or near the end of the K4 message.

But as I considered the word DEGREES immediately before EASTNORTHEAST, and the word BEARING at the very beginning of K4, the required row and column shift statistics have come together much more promisingly in line with my proposed method. The only logical number to fit in between BEARING and DEGREES is SEVENTY, and indeed the row and column shift statistics support this word in this place as well. Here are the required row and column shift value pairs within the DYAHR-keyed Polybius square that would transform (or mask) BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES into QGIYWIU IEAOKGO TKKCGGX, which then encrypts to OBKRUOX OGHULBS OLIFBBW by a Playfair encryption with each letter paired in a bigram with the corresponding letter in the 2nd half of K4:

22 02 23 02 22 01 31   42 00 11 23 02 30 34   34 14 12 12 02 02 10

My statistical analysis shows these shift values to correspond rather well with the expected frequencies of shift values, and of shift value pairs, that are obtained from the K3 ciphertext according to my method:

0: 10 (expected 9.1)
1: 8 (expected 9.0)
2: 14 (expected 14.4)
3: 6 (expected 6.4)
4: 4 (expected 3.1)

And the shift value pairs, corresponding with the pairs obtained from arranging the K3 ciphertext in a 14x24 array (as in the final step of the actual K3 encryption process) and taking the letter pairs that correspond by a 180 degree rotation (or a vertical and then a horizontal reflection) of the array:

02/20 : 31 pairs in K3 ; 5 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
21/12 : 25 pairs in K3 ; 2 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
22 : 16 pairs in K3 ; 2 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
23/32 : 16 pairs in K3 ; 2 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
01/10 : 14 pairs in K3 ; 2 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
31/13 : 12 pairs in K3 ; 1 pair in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
24/42 : 11 pairs in K3 ; 1 pair in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
03/30 : 10 pairs in K3 ; 1 pair in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
11 : 8 pairs in K3 ; 1 pair in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
00 : 7 pairs in K3 ; 1 pair in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
34/43 : 5 pairs in K3 ; 2 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
14/41 : 5 pairs in K3 ; 1 pair in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
04/40 : 4 pairs in K3 ; 0 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
33 : 4 pairs in K3 ; 0 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES
44 : 0 pairs in K3 ; 0 pairs in BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES

Again, these findings remain at the level of striking *statistical* correlations between my proposed method and the possible K4 plaintext BEARING SEVENTY DEGREES EASTNORTHEAST as the first 34 letters of the K4 plaintext message. But I consider that the natural and plausible nature of these possible first 21 letters of the K4 message, given the word EASTNORTHEAST occurring immediately after them, makes this finding worthy of sharing with the main Kryptos group here. As always, I welcome any and all comments, thoughts, questions, criticisms, and other feedback about my findings, my proposed methods, and any of my ideas about Kryptos and the possible K4 encryption/decryption process.

Geoffrey

Good point Sophie, the Memorial Church is a significant Berlin landmark in its own right. In fact, there is an old photo of the Berlin Clock online in its original location, taken in 1979, and the Memorial Church and its belfry are clearly visible in the background.

Brief update: as I stated above, I now believe "X DISTANCE" follows EASTNORTHEAST, which is logical as a statement of distance often follows a statement of bearing with number of degrees and direction. But so far the best fits for my method as K4 plaintext are then rather short distances, less than 100 meters, in order for the number to be written with just 9 English letters after EASTNORTHEAST X DISTANCE and before METERS X FROM BERLIN CLOCK. So "one hundred", "one thousand", or any other number more than 100 would not fit. Possible fits include "seventeen", "twenty one", "twenty two", "twenty six", "forty four", "forty five", "forty nine", and likewise similarly 31, 32, 36, 54, 55, 59, 64, 65, 69, 81, 82, 86, 91, 92, or 96. But it is also possible that the phrase is "three", "seven", "eight", "forty", "fifty", or "sixty" followed by "kiloMETERS". (The last three letters in KILO don't fit my method's statistics well, but just three letters could be a fluke anomaly within a 97-letter text.) For a short distance less than 100 meters ENE, the U-Bahn station entrance could possibly be indicated; for three kilometers it could be a more distant Berlin location in that direction. Of course, the K2 longitude and latitude coordinates point to an obscure location, so it is possible that the K4 bearing and distance directions do the same, and the mystery must still be solved as part of the "K5" puzzle.

Finally, it is more difficult for me to determine the possible text after BERLIN CLOCK, since the possibilities are much more numerous than they are for the first two parts, where my hypothesis of bearing and distance statements narrows down the plausible possibilities. But I have found one candidate phrase after BERLIN CLOCK that makes all the row+column shift value statistics line up well for the 2nd half of K4: "TO THE SILENT". If this is correct, there are then 12 letters remaining in K4, although the 97th and last letter could very well be another "X" to end the statement. In general I think the word "SILENT" fits well within the overall themes of Sanborn's Kryptos sculpture: There is a natural connection between SILENT and the word INVISIBLE in K2, for example. But I have not yet found a good candidate for the word or words after SILENT.

I would be very interested to hear everyone's ideas for what "SILENT" object, item, landmark, location, or other thing in Berlin that Sanborn might possibly be referring to as the other location in K4!

One possible ending of K4 that actually fits the statistical requirements for my method very well is "FROM BERLIN CLOCK TO THE SILENT DROPBOX ABOVE". Now the meaning of this last phrase would be rather obscure, but it may not be completely out of place as one of Sanborn's Kryptos messages, the meanings of which are not expected to be 100% clear at first sight. And it actually kind of fits with Sophie's idea, in her comment in the other thread, about the gaping hole in the old belfry that someone could shine a light into or reach into. Now using the term "dropbox" for this is still kind of strange, but maybe we shouldn't put it past Sanborn or rule it out. The words "silent" and "above" fit well with this church belfry, since its bells are silent after it was bombed.

If this line of thought makes sense, then I have to go back and reconsider the distance measurement in the middle of the K4 message, since the Memorial Church is actually about 700 meters eastnortheast of the Berlin Clock, and my analysis of exactly 9 letters between DISTANCE and METERS allows for three kilometers or longer, which is certainly too long for this measurement, or for ninety-six meters or shorter, which is clearly too short. Perhaps we could justify omitting a single "E" from the entire K4 message, as in DESPARATLY, and make room for 10 letters before METERS. This would allow room for SIX HUNDRED METERS or perhaps even SEVEN HECTOMETERS. (A hectometer is a rather rarely used but technically correct term for 100 meters in the metric system.)

I have an update and a new idea which may make more sense than "SILENT DROPBOX ABOVE", which I must admit was kind of strange compared to the rest of the message that I proposed:

The statistical correlation with my method also works extremely well for the message ending "SILENT BELL TOWERS XX". Clearly this is an excellent description of the Memorial Church's old belfry. But the curious and mysterious part is that the plural word TOWERS is the best fit, particularly with the need to complete the 97-letter message of K4. Yes, I could fudge it one more step with TOWER XXX and it is still an extremely good statistical fit, but I don't like the idea of three X's to pad the end of the message, it just looks like too much of a fudge factor and I don't think Sanborn would have done that. Two X's to conclude the final message of Kryptos seems more reasonable, an emphatic final stop in contrast with the standard single X throughout Kryptos to indicate a stop or end of a sentence.

So then the question becomes, what additional silent bell tower or towers in Berlin could Sanborn possibly be referring to? I would appreciate any ideas from group members.

The other issue, as I mentioned in my previous comment, is that the THREE KILOMETERS distance simply does not work at all from the Memorial Church to any of the Berlin clocks that anyone has proposed. Now it is possible to alter the distance measurement letters and still get a rather very good statistical fit with my method, for example DISTANC SIX HUNDRED METERS. Indeed this works better statistically with BELL TOWERS XX than it did with DROPBOX ABOVE, which may be a good sign. My calculation of the walking distance was closer to 700 meters, but perhaps the most direct distance "as the crow flies" could be shortened enough for it to be within reasonable range to round down to 600 meters. (There is no room in such a short 97-letter message for the minutely detailed precise measurements such as degrees, minutes, and decimal seconds provided in the much longer K2 message.) The omission of the "E" at the end of DISTANC could be justified as comparable to the misspelling of DESPARATLY in K3.

One more general point in favor of this approach despite the technical difficulties: I would actually not expect a K4 message that was so clear that there is nothing mysterious or curious left after reading it! If the references to "BERLIN CLOCK" and "SILENT BELL TOWER" and also the exact distance from the one location to the other were plainly and obviously 100% accurate and correct, that might actually be *too* good to be the K4 message. Too straightforward. We know that there is supposed to be a "K5" that remains to be solved after K4 is solved. The solution of K2 raises as many questions as it answers. So I do not mind a certain amount of mystery in the complete K4 plaintext message, as long as it seems to make logical sense as a message. Still, I would like to have some idea about what Sanborn may have had in mind with the bearing and distance measurements in the message, and if plural SILENT BELL TOWERS is correct, I would like to at least have some candidates for other such bell towers in Berlin in addition to the famous Memorial Church.

s: K4 - Digrams, Word Components and Breaking Assumptions
t:
There is a tendency to interpret information, particularly the written word, in a way that makes the most sense, a sort of natural linguistic confirmatory bias. The best example is Telegram, which reinvented how language is transmitted before becoming obsolete.  Assumed punctuation and sentence structure being merely a piece. We have a lot of assumptions about the structure of K1 to K3 solutions, and those don’t even contain the standard STOP methods  or real punctuation other than a presumed meaning of X. There's even apparent sentence fragments - X LAYER TWO?

Here I’m looking at the Morse Stones, specifically. We automatically interpret them as words whose meaning is meant to be divined.  But perhaps they’re something more literalistic? Like keystones and markers, digrams and cryptograms that can be plotted with pencil in paper if you’re feeling old-school or on a spreadsheet for best effect. So…

VIR-TUAL-LY IN-VI-SIBLE
SIBLE is a special sequence – it’s a repeated pattern that meets the Kasiski Test for Vigenere, and when VISIBLE plaintext is plotted on an x24 Array of Rows & Columns that it helps establish, results in a set of columns that showing BERLIN and NYPVT as a clue within Kryptos and outside of Sanborn’s real world offerings. Moreover, it becomes multiple  playable cryptogram that turns DYAHR into a Caesar Shift of SIBLE, VIR as a Caesar shift of OBK and reveals a massive Acrostic cryptogram  on the borders of x24.

DIG-ET-AL INTERPRET-AT-U
This is read as a misspelled word, when it makes a lot more sense as component parts – DIG, after all, is a part of K4, and when plotted on its own Array, creates formations that could be considered markers to verify that the Array is a correct choice. That’s an extremely important feature – we can guess all we want at Arrays, but unless it shows us something new and meaningful, it’s just speculation.

LUC-ID MEMO-RY
This two is part of the VI-SIBLE columns as are all of the misspellings. LUC is an anagram of CLU, as are KLU (K4) and QLU, and part of a series of ID (identity) based cryptogram clues that all point to the King Tut/Nefertiti’s Tomb theme. MEMO is the Array that K4 is meant to use, and RY is part of the DYAHR cryptogram. Utilized with…

QR/RY
… it becomes the link between K3 ending and K4’s MEMO Array two-character first line and as a visual exercise, makes K4 an addendum to K1-K3. Most important, it sets up alignments between the K1-K3 plaintext digrams and K4 ciphertext ID at NYPVTT. Again, part of that all important BERLIN clue. CLOCK not included.

SHADOW FOR-CES
A cryptogram for SEC ROW OF DAHS, this keystone is important for establishing the dual-use of L and S that exists in K3 (second row, WW NOS NOHS) and in K4. Breaking it down to components, it also works with…

T IS YOUR POSITION
… and becomes CT IS YOUR POSITION. The aforementioned acrostic also puts three other Acrostic based items into play – CT IS AST BALLOON (digrams), CT IS HROHNL (K3 ciphertext), and CT BOWL RING SE (K4 ciphertext)

SOS
Morse referencing, though it also likely has something to do with the E(AST) sequence in K4.

James

t:
Chaocipher Upates.

Some further improvements got the process down to a 1/2 day for some runs.

All candidate CT/PT alphabets for BERLINCLOCK completed
All candidate CT/PT alphabets for EASTNORTHEAST completed

One member will get a kick out of the following candidate however will be disappointed (as I was!) to find it couldn't complete the ES after DEGRE(ES) as the process exhausted all candidates at that point.
['O', '.', '.', '.', '.', '.', '.', 'L', 'F', '.', 'I', '.', 'U', '.', '.', 'G', '.', 'X', 'S', '.', '.', 'B', 'K', '.', 'H', 'R']
['B', '.', 'R', '.', '.', '.', 'N', 'T', 'V', '.', '.', '.', '.', 'D', '.', 'I', 'Y', '.', '.', 'S', '.', '.', 'E', 'G', '.', 'A']

BEARING SEVENTY DEGRE

The system is currently crunching the entire run now from EASTNORTHEAST to the end of BERLINCLOCK and everything in between

'FLRV'+'QQPRNGKSS'+'OTWTQSJQSSEKZZWATJKLUDIAWINFB'+'NYPVTT'+'MZFPK'
'EAST'+'NORTHEAST'+'_____________________^vvvv^^^vvvvvvvv'+'BERLIN'+'CLOCK'

We are up to the 'A' in the K4 code above.

The "^" means that we haven't encountered this CT as yet and need to full explore all possible candidate ct/pt alphabets - this is a huge increase in candidates alphabets
The "v" means that we have seen this CT before and when we get to these runs, we get to cull a lot of candidates as they don't produce the target PT.... Stuff speeds up here.
I didn't bother with flagging known PT runs as per the CT above - just wanted a rough indication of orders of magnitude/timings

As you can see above, we've a triple increase at LUD - nothing for it, just have to let it run. The remaining letters after LUD is a reduction cycle as is BERLINCLOCK itself because it contains pre-filled CT characters in the candidate alphabets produced so far...

After that the answer should be known - it could exhaust candidate alphabets during the BERLIN CLOCK cycle, in this case then vanilla Chaocipher (Chaocipher without ct/pt swaps) can be dismissed as the K4 method.

If it completes BERLINCLOCK then the missing letters can be explored in reverse and also all potential PT letter combos between EAST...BERLIN

Not sure on timings as the current ...ZZWA run is looking like 13GB of candidate alphabets however that should get reduced nicely. The LUD run is a complete unknown at this stage...

Cheers, Mike

s: Is/has anyone worked on using GROMARK:?
t: I've been following Kryptos for about 15 years. I always come back to "Is it a GROMARK with some other method?" I can't shake off the fact that GROMARK has been used in some way. Does anyone else have any strong feelings about using GROMARK?

Q Counts

Of the solutions to date only k1 and k3 contain any Q's. Both within one column of each other and both completely "?unnecessary?." One is a misspelling of the word illusion in k1 and the only other Q in the message text is used at the end of k3 as a fill of sorts. This extra letter isn't actually necessary; as a transposition cipher doesn't need even lines. Additionally of interest, is the burning question of why a Q? Any letter could be used as a fill. Why not use a letter frequent within the text.

I have a new theory: each misspelling in the sculpture is a lodestone and each line corresponds to the horizontal (West to East) light-colored brick rows in and around the courtyard. I counted the number of rows and got 28. This includes the 6 or 7 rows on the North and South sides of the courtyard. As far as I can tell, they have been there since 1990. The number of lines in the sculpture is 28. That means that there would be three (not sure if the missing e in the word desparatly would count) lodestones in (or around) the courtyard area. There is already one lodestone at the entrance. If my theory were true, the bird pond is where one would need to be to figure out the last message. All they would need to do is horizontally run a compass across the stone slabs around the pond and figure out what direction is a dot and what direction is a dash. This would be similar to the “Invisible Forces” art piece by Jim Sanborn: https://www.elonka.com/kryptos/sanborn/forces.html. Maybe the misspellings were put there so that someone who wasn’t there could still transpose the four messages onto the courtyard brick rows and figure out the locations of the hidden lodestones. Wouldn’t that explain why there is a compass engraved onto the stone slab at the entrance with a lodestone there? I think the bird pond slabs contain hidden Morse that will only reveal itself when using a compass there. I wonder if each square brick would count as a letter and that is how you determine spacing in order to figure out the locations of the hidden lodestones (if they exist).

Like many of you, I have been working on Kryptos for a long time. In my case, for 18 years. Like most who had not read or heard any of Jim Sanborn's interviews, I was puzzled when he made seemingly conflicting or possibly misleading statements when talking about Kryptos. This situation caused me to not be able to move forward in the game very far. In fact, I would still be in a state of confusion if I hadn't read what Sanborn had said in one of his interviews.

In the 2005 CNN interview, he said, "... I seem to like to manipulate the information coming out, in a sort of disinformation fashion. Which seems appropriate for the project. And so, a lot of the clues that I might give work in a sort of disinformational way, and that's a good thing. I mean, that's clandestine ethos."
Now armed with that piece of knowledge, in time I found that, unless Sanborn is specifically revealing something about solving Kryptos, I should not assume anything about what he said beyond his specific words. As an example:
Sanborn specified the string BERLINCLOCK as being plaintext residing in positions corresponding to positions 64 to 74 in the K4 CT. I ask you, with this information only, what is the first possible inference you would detect about it? You might have assumed that BERLINCLOCK was a piece of the final solution of K4. But, Sanborn did not say that it was part of the final solution. He only said that it was plaintext (which it is) and that it lies in positions corresponding to positions 65 to 75 of the K4 CT. So, if you assumed BERLINCLOCK was part of the final solution to K4, you shouldn't have, since BERLINCLOCK is something else. It is part of the keyword THEBERLINCLOCK. Now, since I have not yet arrived at the final solution to K4, I can't say whether BERLINCLOCK is part of it, and lying in positions 64 to 74 in the final solution, but my gut says it isn't. Rest assured that I don't consider it being even remotely possible.
Now, having said all that, I need to say also that if I detect an inference about something, I know that I must attempt to find out that which is being inferred and act on it. K2 PT is full of clues to do this, and even to the point of blatantly saying it. Example: "... WHO KNOWS THE EXACT LOCATION". This says WHO NO S, THE X A CT LOCATION, to place the S in the 9th position which will make the X appear in the CT. The WHO part provides another clue via the WAS grammar error pointing to the S in the middle of the

N L SL S LS L N box. The W in WHO is the W of the WAS grammar error and the S of WAS is in the center of the box.
So, I guess I need to warn those who continue to believe that K4 will be solved solely via cryptographic manipulation. K4 is full of tricks and clues reside in a lot of places.
PaulK

I absolutely agree that the things Jim & Ed say are to be taken with a large grain of salt. When some of us met at Ed's house (2017?) my question to him was (approximately) "Do you guys play this like a game of 20 questions, where what you tell us is technically true, but put as misleadingly as possible?", and his answer, of course, was "We don't deliberately mislead you." Unfortunately the locals we have encountered on this particular island decline to belong to tribes which consistently tell either truth or lies, so we must sift & weigh the best we can.

In looking over the posted transcripts of interviews with Ed, I note that in one of them he gives the impression that he showed Jim perhaps a half-dozen techniques, made sure Jim understood them, then told Jim, You've got what you need, go do your thing -- and presumably retired from the scene. On the other hand, at the meeting in the spy museum (2013?), while other people were talking to Jim and Ed, I chatted up Ed's son and heard (again approximately) as follows: Son really has no idea what Dad used for the K4 message. Knowing Dad, he conjectures it might well be some ancient historical thing translated into English. Son does remember Dad out on the deck working over the thing for many hours, over many days, thinks Dad enjoyed himself greatly. (Carl doesn't doubt it.) These two versions of the degree of Ed's involvement do not seem to me to square. If Kryptos is inter alia to teach young Company men about their jobs, surely part of what it wants to teach them is to never get too overconfident that your trusty & proven sources will ~always~ tell you the truth, even when they know it. I'm pretty sure ours don't always overdo the candor bit.

But as to "Plaintext", my understanding of the word is that it means the deciphered text which the intended recipient is intended to understand, and ~not~ some coincidence or intermediate artifact of the system, which does not appear in the intended decryption. I think calling something of that sort "plaintext" would amount to a straightforward, whopping, recommended-by-Kipling lie, which doesn't seem their style. Maybe they resort even to that in a pinch, but my bet is that BERLINCLOCK will appear right where we're told it will in the midst of 97 letters of legible, non-gibberish English. (Tho maybe it will be a further allusion to something else, a bit of true code under the cipher, like Ed's "cake" meaning "meet me tomorrow at 1500") Matter of fact, Paul, I will bet literally, and I'll give you odds: I'll put up an official portrait of Ben Franklin against your portrait of Grant, bet's off if either of us croaks before K4 breaks. Am I on? >:)

But back to agreeing with you. It is full of tricks, and I suspect a lot of cryptanalysts are going to feel a bit cheated when they find out just how much of K4 is not standard cryptography. We were warned tho, that it is a unique kind of a critter, and Ed is mainly interested in our methodology. E.g., I herewith submit one of my theoretical findings:

1. Write out deciphered K2 in separate sentences so that you will see it.

It was totally invisible

How's that possible ?

They used the earth's magnetic field X

The information was gathered and transmitted
undergruund to an unknown location X

Does Langley know about this ?

They should, it's buried out there somewhere X

Who knows the exact location ?

Only WW - this was his last message X

"Thirty-eight degrees, fifty-seven minutes, six point five
seconds North, seventy-seven degrees, 8 minutes, forty-
four seconds West" X

ID by rows (as sculpted) Layer two ("corrected")

OK, what's missing? You can see why it's totally invisible - Jim didn't carve it there. The second missing "period" is a 'teachable moment' kind of thing, sort of nudging us to notice the first; since the first sentence made sense, we might not otherwise look closely at it.

2. How does Carl corroborate this notion to himself? (Scott Perry did the work , and I thank him.) YA H R are the 4th, 5th, 6th & 7th letters of K3, 4+5+6+7 = 22. In the string found by Scott, when BERLIN is moved to the same position which it is supposed to occupy in the PT, beginning at place 22 is the word JAIL. And lest we might say "Ah, four letters isn't much, that's a meaningless coincidence" we are given an extra "L" after the "J" on line 15 of the tableau, just to incline us to have JL / JAIL on our minds. Sort of a homonym. And we can come up with another, JAEL. I know Jim is an atheist, or agnostic, whatever, and doesn't like religion dragged into his work, but if he puts it in himself I don't think he can complain. Maybe Ed did it. Anyway JAEL is Hebrew for what we call an ibex. And I conclude that "I be X " is to go at spot number 22 of K2, and as "It was totally invisible" amounts to 21 letters, there's the missing period. Doubtless looks rubbery to others, but Carl is a bit gullible.

3. But we're not supposed to need to have broken K1-K3 to do any of the breaking of K4, it's just that what we find may be helpful. So how do we know to do this otherwise, how does Jim come back 20 years later and do the necessary without all kinds of deciphering? D YA H R. D is the 3rd letter - interpret the digits as 3 & 22: Third Line, Spot 22 , add X .

4. Why ? Suppose that the system for K4 is to take a part of the rest of the sculpture, transpose the hell out of it until the 'washing machine' has made it essentially a random sequence of 97 letters, add that to the K4 PT and take the Mod 26 of the result, or use the random sequence against the Tableau for some form of Quag or Beaufort. The washing machine has to be defined somehow for Jim, and it has to be defined by clues for us. But the 'load of laundry', so to speak, has got to be just the right size and in the right configuration to fit those clues, or the additive sequence won't work. In this scenario, an extra letter here or there is critical. It seems we are pointed to line 3, spot 22, but how many more additions need to be made? Does WW get his abbreviating 'periods' too, now that we have the idea?

A theory. And a long way from proof by producing a K4 PT. But the main point is that this kind of thing is going to get us further than classic crypto techniques.

Carl Ellis

P.S. - Wonder what the Tarot might have to say about all this. A little sober, scientific research is indicated after all ...

P.P.S. - My thanks to Sophie French and Wondered Things, looks like I should get hold of Mr. Khalid Sheikh at U. of Houston.

There are three Assumptions about Kryptos that immediately come to mind.
1.    That “L” is on the outside rim of the Kryptos tableaux.
2.    That the plaintext is irrelevant to Sanborn’s indicated clues.
3.    That the solution to K4 is a proper cipher, known or invented.

I mention the first despite it’s apparent irrelevancy, primarily because it’s such a great example of major assumptions that have permeated Kryptos discussion to a degree that all known references, including the CIA page, show “L” on the outer rim and the Vigenere Tableaux in a normal state. The actual Sculpture text is that of a reversed tableaux and the “L” acting as a bridge between K4 and the Tableaux.  That’s pure assumption couched as casual iron-clad fact to the point where people have argued when it is pointed out, despite examination of the sculpture pictures showing exactly that.

#2 is where we have a full forest of ideas that present questions answered by Sanborn and Scheidt as fact.
You have one person who has an amateur’s knowledge of a subject.
You have a second who is an expert, but only offered ideas to the first and didn’t train them and wasn’t really involved.
And that is why it is spot on to take with a grain of salt their answers to a bunch of very clever people quizzing them separately in hopes of getting clues.

Here’s one I’ve never liked.

“We’re not supposed to have solved K1 to K3….”

…. And yet one can simply stumble across a bunch of simple K4 cryptograms by the pure accident of how the rows are arranged and using the Stones as a help aid. You can stumble across it, not have any clue why it’s there or what it’s for unless you’ve found other existing PT and CT clues first.
You have a technically true answer that is not the whole truth. No lie, no misdirection. Just not all of it.

For the sake of that side topic, I’ll note here that I don’t recall ever hearing the words “supposed to” here. Only the answer that it’s not entirely necessary. i.e. the short way of luck vs the long way of clue exploration.

Regarding your first point: Some misdirection was brought on by Jim's leaving the "extra L" off the mini-sculpture that he had up for sale. This caused some people to assume that their conclusions that the "extra L" was indeed an error on the main sculpture because Jim eliminated it on the mini. This is an excellent example of bringing attention to a clue and also of misdirection. Of course, we are not just talking about the L at the end of the line. We also notice that both the beginning of the row and the end of the row have the same series of five letters, GHIJL. This makes the row special, as the same thing does not occur on any other row in the tableau. There is a clue pointing to this in the K4 CT. It's the letters GHUL. This is a mini-stego trick that looks like GHIJL. And, I propose to you that this is not all. The K4 string continues to GHULB. The ULB part is the reverse of BLU, refering to the JOHNNY NASH (remember the talk a while back about his song, "I Can See Clearly Now"?) words BLUE SKIES and SUNSHINY DAY. Notice the string continues... GHULBSOL. The SUN! I think you will see that all of this is not something being pulled out of a hat. It sort of reminds of the mini-sculpture that appeared on Ed's table when he met with some of the group. The GIRASOL sculpture. The GIRASOL cipher is related to all that. I'm still working on figuring out all that's hidden in the GIRASOL cipher, but it has revealed a lot of clues about Kryptos, many of which I had already discovered in Kryptos and some of which caused me to be able to move past unseen obstacles that could not have been perceived otherwise. This is an example of one of the sources of clues outside of Kryptos itself. All related to that lonely L at the end of the row. Look at Ivans Find.pdf in my personal folder to see one way the extra L row comes into play.
The plaintext is relevant, and sometimes two or more meanings can be applied to a string of text.
As I have said before, there may be more than one way to solve K4, but I have found only one so far, and it is not just a simple cipher.

PaulK

PS. The bottom left corner of the TAROT card is the bottom right corner of something else. Interesting times. :)

While it’s nice to have a series of clues involving the Greek Underworld and provable cryptograms involving the Egyptian over-world bound neatly together in a celestial sphere  by themes and THEBES that mirrors the Urania World Clock, it’s even nicer to have something that puts them together in a way that is meaningful to cracking K4.

This requires a little explanation.

As noted, there’s a number of phonemic cryptograms such as NYPVTT (Nefertiti) that circle around the King Tut side of the theme. If we treat –NYT- as one of them, it becomes NIGHT, which is important in several ways, particularly the I-QLUS (eye clues). That is, the eyes of King Tut’s headdress represent clocks – one eye is the passage of Horus’s solar-barge through the hours of day, while the other represents the passage of his night vessel through the 12 hours of night. There is of course a Gnomon on the front of the ship, and a whole history that goes with it. The night-boat is referred to as MESKETET or MSKTT.
Like these clocks, Caesar Shifts can be considered as day and night – A and Z represent the twilight exchange, and the 24 hours between split evenly into day and night.

In addition to this important concept is the name of the night-boat, which explains the 24-Array CT acrostic that has long defied explanation for me – what I assumed was BUST KWOTE. It would appear that instead, it is a word play:   SEK-TUT BOW – the bow of MESEKTET is the gnomon on the eye-clock.
A second clue supporting the first from Sanborn’s handwritten PT on a reversed 42-Array.

James

Now that Jim Sanborn seems to have backed off from confirming a 1-to-1 correspondence between plaintext characters and ordinally equivalent ciphertext characters, it may indeed be interesting to check out one’s old notes and see if there’s anything that may presently be seen in a different light.

When revisiting my previous attempts to tackle the mythical “masking technique”, I found notes about my following unravelling attempt:

1)    Let’s take the last three lines of Kryptos K4, which are exactly 31 characters long each.
2)    Set up a Quagmire 2 (<not> a Quagmire 3!) with primary key KRYPTOS and the following indicator key of exactly 31 characters: “KRYPTOSABCDEFGHIJLMNQUVWXZKRYPT” (following the pattern of the tabula recta).
3)    Line by line, decrypt with the Quagmire 2 set up above.

Then the resulting matrix looks as follows:

VEWCJJPKAXVGDZUTHVZICZYGDUNZEDB
EWCRCLOZYCQONKTPAJZCQULARUMHRZZ
WDCPVHXTPEAPNLQBTTXUGASYJWLZHEX

So, what’s in it? There are three observations, the last of which may be relevant in the light of Jim Sanborn’s recent comments:

A)    Emanating from the tip of the upper left-hand corner, and going out both in the horizontal and the vertical direction, there’s the very same trigram (VEW). Admittedly, the letters of that trigram don’t create any “wow!” effect as a “YAR” would, but the symmetry is somehow nice and (at least to me) unexpected.

B)    In the upper left-hand corner area, there’s a trigram repeat (of EWC) at a distance of 30 characters. Under the speculation that the elusive masking technique has been removed (and that there’s still a 1-to-1 correspondence), this could indicate a final substitution step to take. With the plaintext known today, period lengths of 5, 10 and 15 can be quickly ruled out (hope that my notes don’t deceive me here), but a period of 30 characters just might be possible (my attempts in that direction led nowhere).

C)    Now this is an observation that’s only of interest if transposition is still in the game (as it now seems to be): The resulting matrix contains the fragment CLO in the next to last line, which could be seen as the start of the known plaintext word CLOCK. The resulting matrix also contains bigrams EA, TH and BE that are found in known plaintext. Could there be some transposition involved? Obviously, however, the overall character frequencies are not consistent with the English language (thus failing the test mentioned by Elonka in message #22810), so it’s certainly a long shot.

All in all, the artefact described above probably owes its characteristics to the workings of chance, but I still consider it to be somehow out of the ordinary, especially in the context of Jim Sanborn’s recent statements.

By the way, all the best wishes to Jim Sanborn on his 76th birthday!

Perhaps Sukhwant meant to say that the original *intended* location of the Kryptos sculpture was planned to be at the coordinates provided by JS. Sanborn of course had to compose and finalize all of the messages well in advance before the actual physical construction of the sculpture itself. So perhaps he included those coordinates in the message *thinking* that he was simply specifying the location of the sculpture itself. Plans can change, details can change, and it is possible that there was no way to go back and change the message itself at the time that the exact intended location and placement of the sculpture was changed for whatever reason. The latter would have been a CIA decision, not a Sanborn decision, and there may have been nothing Sanborn could do about it, or about the messages he composed, at the time such a decision was made.

Please note: I have no idea if any of this actually happened. I am simply suggesting a plausible possibility based on Sukhwant's comment.

I commented some months ago on a solution path, but didn’t get much comment at the time. I’ll give it another go.

“Mask” is a cute and helpful and slightly misleading clue - especially given that Howard Carter discovered one of the most iconic masks in human history during his excavations. He wrote about it in his 28 Oct 1925 field journal entry, and I identify a portion of that entry as the likely book key to start off the K4 solution.

The K4 technique is: take the correct book passage, transpose it in a manner similar to K3, trim out the unnecessary letters (the passage is a bit too long), and use the result as a substitution key for the final stage. It’s a neat and tidy “final boss” puzzle using the same skills we’ve seen already, just in combination and with an extra degree of difficulty.

The passage I’ve identified as the key is:

THE PINS REMOVED, THE LID WAS RAISED. THE PENULTIMATE SCENE WAS DISCLOSED - A VERY NEATLY WRAPPED MUMMY OF THE YOUNG KING WITH GOLDEN MASK OF SAD BUT TRANQUIL EXPRESSION SYMBOLIZING OSIRIS.

The passage is 154 letters long, which is 97 + 57. 57 is a nice number to see, because it’s in the puzzle twice already - as one of the geography numbers, and as the letter position of the “iQlusion” spelling.

“THE PINS” fits neatly into the upper left of K3, creating a visual idea of a key fitting a lock and raising the tumbler pins. This may also help identify where to locate the 57 extraneous characters for removal. I have an idea of a transposition matrix of 8 columns by ~19 rows, with rows corresponding to the raised “pins” being removed. But I haven’t fully worked that out yet.

Aside from the 57 math, the end of the source key is also signaled by the X and Q at the end of K3 (which are separated by 17 letters). Find the X and Q words, then continue 17 letters.

And I hope it’s obvious that “HIS MUMMY!” is the answer any bright 12-year old would give if asked what Carter saw inside King Tut’s tomb!

—

EASTNORTHEAST -> RDUMRIYWOYNKY

Soooo, I reckon that I subconsciously saw the pattern & just grabbed it or, more likely, it was a total fluke!

Either way I’m impressed with the calibre of the group in spotting this pattern either way :)

Kind Regards, Mike

s: Nefertiti = an interesting clock in Berlin?
t:
As we know, Jim Sanborn has said "there are several interesting clocks in Berlin"... and we're not sure exactly which "clock" he's referring to. Of course clock means "timekeeping device". But there are several other meanings too (thanks, thesaurus.com). My favorite is "face [noun] front of something; expression, exterior".

What if the famous "Berlin Clock" is the face/bust of Nefertiti?

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nefertiti_Bust

Some supporting arguments to this theory:
- Obvious ties to King Tut & Egypt (K3)
- It is in Berlin (controversially)
- Various textual Egypt/Queen/etc. "clues" (maybe) --> see my file "nefertiti1.pdf" in JBONSALL folder
- Her missing left eye could be "buried out there somewhere"

Just a thought, and obviously it's a stretch... but whether or not she's the "clock", I think she is hidden in the puzzle for some reason.

-Jamie

PS yes, I know, Scheidt's driveway seemingly has a Mengenlehreuhr on it... do we violate Occam's razor and claim this is just misdirection? :)

s: Q? Highly Skewed One's and Zero's
t:
Hi all,

Question for the K4 binary theorists out there (inc. oneself):

There was a mention in one of the dinner notes (Ed Scheidt, October 21, 2007)  re "evening out the 1's and 0's" - Baudot/Murray, Morse and Gray all "seem" to do that naturally with the possible exception of Gray due the the in-stream hardware error correction considerations...

* So why should the one's and zeros be so skewed to require further treatment?

* Was it the Sanborn's K4 encoding method or the just quirk of Sanborn's text after conversions to one of the above mappings pre masking?

I've gone back to 5-bit whilst Chaocipher runs to ground + all the extraneous clues yell "digital interpretation" anyhows and XOR (L. RAhY/light/shadows/subtle shading, or even 'R' and 'Y')

Also, I'm looking at throwing "OBKR" out as part of K4 proper - I'm leaning towards OBKR as being a hint to method as per ("He described one case where he wanted the recipient to be able to receive a message 10 years after being taught the technique, and be able to "eyeball the message" to find hints to remind him how to decode it.")

So that just leaves 3 x 31 to crack...

Thoughts?...

Mike

Have gone back to 5-bit binary whilst waiting any Chaocipher insights, was never sure if a non-binary solution as in scope., will see what is reveles re  new stat count for other stuff...

t:
Cool idea Mike. That got me thinking, what if the L->Q and O->U "mistakes" in IQLUSION and UNDERGRUUND are suggesting how the "masking technique" works? And the letters in dYAhR are part of the "algorithm"? That would be quite interesting....

I whipped up a quick spreadsheet demonstrating this... it's in my personal folder (JBONSALL), it's called ascii flip.pdf. My idea is take the first 8 characters of K3 endYAhRo, and YAR corresponds to a bitflip and the other characters do not flip.

Result is: the O->U "mistake" is an exact match for this! If you bit-flip the ASCII for "O", you get "U".

But the L->Q "mistake" is not an exact match, so that may be unrelated, or suggesting another part of the "algorithm"...

I'll be playing with this some more :)

-Jamie

s: Possible use of German key phrase - Berlin Peace Clock
t:
I've been interested in considering K4 from a non-standard ways.

It occurs to me that there are combinations of letters which almost form meaningful German words. The words here form part of the letters which are skewed.  Admittedly, I'm clutching at straws here, but hear me out.

The first line of K3 CT reads as follows

EndyaHroHNLSRHEOCPTEOIBIDYSHNAIA

Endy => Ende => End
aHr => uhr => clock
oHNLS => without
ruhe => rest,quiet

From my own investigations, the minimum length vingenere key to decode K4 is 26 characters in length, as without a single key of this length or greater, the resulting plaintext cannot recover the cribs EAST NORTHEAST BERLIN and CLOCK

The last line in K2, directly above the K3 text shown above, is as follows:

DQUMEBEDMHDAFMJGZNUPLGEWJLLAETG

 Considering the ID BY WEST and LAYER TWO error in this text, I'm suspecting that the German phrase may start on the K2 line, not the K3 line.

I'm only using Google translate to deduce possible words here, but a simple phrase like "ein Ende der Uhr ohne ruhe" becomes "an end of the clock with no rest".  Yes, again I admit I'm clutching at straws, but remember this cryptext is also used to encrypt two separate phrases.  The premise I'm proposing is that the mistakes in the K1 (IQLUSION), K2 (UNDERGRUUND, ID BY WEST / LAYER TWO) and K3 (DESPARATLY) produce a recipe to repair the phrase.

Can anyone see possible german words in the lines:

DQUMEBEDMHDAFMJGZNUPLGEWJLLAETG
ENDYAHROHNLSRHEOCPTEOIBIDYSHNAIA

Cheers,

Ian

s: Clues From Handwritten Charts of K1/K2
t:
Hello All.

From the following reference:

http://www.thekryptosproject.com/kryptos/charts/all.php

A couple years ago I spent time reviewing Sanborn's handwritten charts which he used to write the original PT/CT (which I believe to have certainly been released publicly to assist in solving K4), and always noticed two interesting things which I am not sure have been pointed out before, and have been unable to implement thus far towards a solution:

1. There are five lines which contain a sentence ending with "X" in K2. In the presented format on the handwritten charts, if you count the number of characters on each line after each "X", they add up to 93. Including the X from each row would add up to 98 (Line 5 "X" has 25 following characters, Line 7 "X" has 17 following, Line 9 has 17, Line 11 has 26, and Line 14 has 8, so 25+17+17+26+8 = 93 + 5 "X"s = 98 Characters). Taking this information into account with the fact that Sanborn "left off" a character from line 14..... 98 - 1 missing character = 97 characters. I have tried OTP methods with these 97 characters over the last couple years, but nothing productive.

2. The locations of the two misspellings (I"Q"LUSION and "UNDERGR"U"UND) have been stated before as being of importance, vice the letters involved. If you pad the PT or CT from K1 and K2 into the same line lengths (31) as presented in the handwritten charts, including the line 5 oddity and leaving the "N" from "illusion" out of the line count as in the photos, the locations of the misspelled "Q" (and associated CT) and misspelled "U" (and associated CT) form a perfect 5x5 square as follows:

PT -

EO F IQ
HOWST
THSMA
ASGAT
UUNDT

and CT -

YQTMK
QETGF
GPFXH
JUNGE
ETBJD

This might be of interest to anyone working a Playfair or otherwise using a 5x5 grid for solving.

Hopefully this post contains some utility to someone and is not a repeat of previous observations posted.

t:
Well, as an alternative to interpreting AHR as Uhr, YAHR has always struck me as close to Jahr = year. ENDYAHR => "Endyear".

Furthermore, I've always felt that HEOCPTE sort of shouts "helicopter" and DQUMEBED suggests "document(ed)"... however that would be more English than German.

I don't necessarily think it has significance, but in this context I might as well mention it.

I'm sorry about the delayed reply to this one.

I would like to elaborate on the fact that "KRY" appears near the end of Jon's step-7 alphabet. Interestingly, it is preceded by "PWD" (password), but I'm not pursuing that in particular.

You may find it amusing/interesting that if you take every 4th letter of the normal alphabet you get the following two 13-letter alphabets containing the odds and the evens, respectively (and this partitioning happens because 2 is a common factor of 4 and 26):

AEIMQUYCGKOSW
BFJNRVZDHLPTX

Near the end you see PT and OS. So using step-7 and step-4 alphabets you can glue together the word "KRYPTOS" from three fragments taken from these alphabets.

There is another curiosity here:

Infamously, decrypting NYPVTTMZFPK to BERLINCLOCK using exactly the same method as in K1 and K2, we get the reconstructed keystream ELYOIECBAQK. If the same is done assuming standard Vigenére, using the normal alphabet instead of the Kryptos one, we get MUYKLGKORNA (this is also well known).

The curiosity is the similarity between the first step-4 alphabet and the latter keystream.
M_UY_GKO vs  MUY__GKO.

I find no similar curiosity with EASTNORTHEAST.

Hi LouiZSA,

The separation of OBKR is starting to appear more like a key to the method to use to decode the remaining 3x31 however am not sure what to make of it yet. Is it "digital" or just a reminder to the recipient as to the (four?) steps required for decoding K4.

Also, those remaining 93 characters can only be reshaped as 3x31 or 31x3 - which makes the number of potential L3-like manipulations limits to just those two shapes, and that is a good place to be :)

Example: 3x31 --> rotate 90 degrees (31x3) --> rotate 90 degrees (3x31)

Back from (Ed Scheidt, October 21, 2007 Elonka's meeting notes):

* Ed mentioned he has 15 patents
* He described one case where he wanted the recipient to be able to receive a message 10 years after being taught the technique, and be able to "eyeball the message" to find hints to remind him how to decode it.

I checked his patents and did catch the following many times in different patents from the 90's:
“The encrypted CKM header is concatenated to the beginning of the encrypted data to form transmit data, and the packet header and the transmit data are concatenated to form a transmit packet.”

CKM stands for CryptoKi Mechanism as part of the PKCS system where PKCS stands for "Public Key Cryptography Standards". The highest "method" value I've come across so far is 4002 --> 0100,0000,0000,0010 - so there is a precedence there as well is as with standard computer file headers...

IMHO, I don't think Sanborn would have gone all the way down the full modern crypto path but the concept of adding an encoded method/hint to the beginning of the payload makes sense in light of Scheidt's comments

So yep, I will keep in mind "BOX E" when looking at those remaining 93 letters :)

Hmmm. just about to hit send and thought of  "Box by 5"

And, funny enough, re those character counts:

* K's has the highest count in K4.

* When you convert English letter frequencies into ITA-2/Baudot you get 60% zero's and 40% ones. The easiest steps I've found to get those stats to near 50:50 (in fact, 52:48) is top swap the E (12.7 % of chars) and the K (0.7% of chars) symbols around!

Good find.

Cheers, Mike

s: K4 3x31 Rotated Right by 90 Degrees then Re cast to 3x31
t:
Hi all,

Not sure if any of the below has been observed/posted before - just getting it out as a handy reference + highlight a few exciting things :)

* K4 without OBKR i.e. the last 3 lines can only be reshaped as 3 x 31 or 31 x 3
* We can rotate that 90 degrees to the right and always reshape back to 3 x 31, as per one of the K3 solutions (see my Python Notebook for a coded demo)
* 24, yes 24!, such rotations brings us back to the starting position - so full circle in 24 steps - this ties in nicely with the "GIRASOL" hint/24 hours
* The Letter "T" remains in a fixed position throughout the transforms in the centre - "T is your position" as would any character at position 47/93

* means that NYPVTT --> BERLIN isn't strictly 1:1 unless all rotations go through...
* any number of intermediate manipulates, binary or otherwise, could have occurred along the way - perhaps keyed to the "hour"
* perhaps the spare "L" now becomes the hand of a clock and maybe means the "hour" to do some other manipulation e.g. 3,9,15,21

Kind Regards, Mike

s: Help Wanted -- Producing a Running Key
t:
I need some help.
I'm working on an idea that K4 is Vigenere with a running key.
Consider three 5x21 matrices, one for plaintext, one for key, and one for ciphertext.
When Jim provided cribs, here merely read out row 4 (BERLINCLOCK) and leter row 2 (EASTNORTHEAST).
Those cribs give us 11+13= 24 letters of key which we can place in the Key Matrix.
One can think of traditional Vigenere (as with K1 and K2) as using 3 matrices, where the Key matrix is filled with a repeating Keyword (e.g., PALIMPSEST).  The weakness of this is that if you know/guess the keyword length, you can reduce the problem to a set of simple substitutions.  Ed talked about this at length, where in K1/K2 we had the advantage of knowledge of statistical properties (English letter frequencies).  For K4, he "took this away" and "did something to mask the statistical information".  Note that he never used the term "masking step" but merely "did something".
One thing he could do is to use a random Key Matrix, which would turn this into a one time pad and no solution is possible.  The operational problem with one time pads is they are hard to use:  you need to convey all the random key letters reliably.
So what else could he do to create a Key matrix that doesn't have repeating patterns?  One possibility is he could start with a Key Matrix with a known pattern, and encrypt it to form a pseudo random pattern for the final Key Matrix.
Where else do we see a 5x21 matrix?  Look at the last 4 columns of the KRYPTOS tableau, plus the extra L.  That's 105 letters, and they are almost uniformly distributed (4 of each Key letter, plus an extra L).
Suppose he took those 105 letters, copied them into a 105 letter matrix (e.g., using the factors 3,5,7 to form matrices such as 3x35, 15x7,etc.) and then encrypted that matrix to end up with a 5x21 letter matrix used to Vig encrypt the Plaintext Matrix.  If he used transposition (a la K3) he would maintain the uniform distribution of Key letters providing a good basis for encrypting the plaintext.
While there are a lot of Transposition methods, the one he taught to Jim used rotating matrices.  That leaves small number fo possibilities using matrix sized 5x21, 21x5, 15x7, 7x15, 35x3, 3x35.
If our Plaintext Matrix has EASTNORTHEAST at the start of row 2, and BERLINCLOCK at the start of row 4,

K3 is a 336 letter ciphertext generated as a transposition of the K3 plaintext.
The mapping of plaintext to ciphertext can be performed via a simple linear congruential generator:
Xi = a Xi-1 + b mod n where X0 is 250, a is 1, b is 251, and n is 337.  This is a maximal length generator which generates all the numbers in 0..336, and where 336 maps to itself and we just just 0..335 for the 336 letters.
i=0   250  CT[0] = PT[250] = E
i=1   164  CT[1] = PT[164] = N
i=2    78  CT[2] = PT[78] = D
i=3   329  CT[3] = PT[329] = Y
The inverse (for decryption) is Xi = a Xi-1 + b mod n, , where X0 is 191, a=1, b= 192, and n = 337.

The transformation can also be performed by rotations of 336 element matrices.  To decrypt, load the ciphertext into a 14x24 matrix, rotate left 90 degrees, copy into a 42x8 matrix, rotate left 90 degrees, read out the resultant 8x42 matrix.
As I recall, we believe this is how Jim created K3, since rotating matrices ("washing machine") is a lot simpler for a guy who claims he can't tell the difference between Modulo and Square Root.

So we have 2 equivalent algorithms for performing the transposition.  Does this work for other messages, or is it unique to K3?
My question: is this a general result:  for any given set of rotations of rectangular matrices, does there exist a corresponding linear congruential generator?
Is there a tutorial somewhere explaining why this works:  e.g, how to determine the LCG that corresponds to the matrix rotation operations?

Hi Doug,

I want to say that LCG was not actually used by Jim Sanborn. As you see, you need an LCG where a = 1. When the multiplier of the LCG is 1 it defeats the purpose. That is because of the multiplicative identity property of 1. Anything multiplied by 1 is itself. So you can just cancel out the multiplier, it is not needed. At that point it is not really LCG anymore. What you end up with is a *simple* equation to count every Nth position, and the modulus operation makes it "wrap around" to the beginning. Xi = Xi - 1 + b mod n.

So what is Xi = Xi - 1 + 192 mod 337 actually doing?

~ With + 192 in the equation you are basically just counting every 192th position.

~ The - 1 in the equation makes the counting 0 based. This is very helpful when you write a program with a language that uses 0 based arrays, where the index of the first item is 0, and the index of the last item is array length - 1. So with K3 that would be 0 to 335. That means starting from Xi = 0 the 192th position is at index 191.

~ The modulus in the equation performs two tasks. (A) it makes it wrap around to the beginning (B) it makes it subtract 1 every time it wraps around. Normally if you wanted to do task (A) only, and keep the index between range 0 to 335, you would just use a modulus of 336. That way when you reach the end index 335 the next step 336 would wrap around to index 0. But in this case we are using modulus of 337 which is (length + 1). This performs task (B) of subtracting 1 when wrapping around. This extra task (B) only works because our step is greater than 1 (our step is 192), and because we start at index 191. Both of which prevents us from landing on index 336 (which doesn't exist) because we always surpass 337, and we stop on index 144 (the Q). The next step after index 144 would be 144 + 192 = 336 which would break because index 336 doesn't exist. Subtracting 1 every time you wrap around is important in this case because otherwise it would iterate through the same positions over and over after the first wrap around.

So now that we know the equation works just by taking every Nth character and subtracting 1 every wrap around, we should better understand what that actually does. Taking every Nth character of the ciphertext is identical to loading the ciphertext into a matrix with a width of N, and rotating it 90 degrees counterclockwise (left).

Think about it, if you have a 5x5 matrix and you take every 5th character, you are taking all the characters from the right side of the matrix vertically, and placing it on top of the new matrix horizontally. That is a 90 degree rotation left. Note: in this example you'd have to subtract 1 every time you wrap around so you don't keep getting the same 5 characters.

For example here is a 5x5 alphabet.

ABCDE
FGHIJ
KLMNO
PQRST
UVWXY

Starting at 0 and taking every 5th means you will take E, J, O, T, Y. Then when you wrap around you subtract 1 and start at the 4th which is D, then every 5th would be I, N, S, X. Then wrap and subtract 1 to start at the 3rd which is C, take every 5th will be H, M, R, W. Rinse and repeat. You end with a 90 degree rotation.

EJOTY
DINSX
CHMRW
BGLQV
AFKPU

Notice A, B, C, D, E is now on the left side vertically.

So here is the fun part. As you know you can decrypt K3 by first putting it into a matrix that has a width of 24 (I call this cutting), then rotating 90 degrees left. Then put it in a matrix with width of 8, then rotate 90 degrees left. That is 24*8=192. That is why taking every 192nd character with LCG works, it is identical to cutting and rotating two times with 24 and 8.

This also works for other products where A*B=192. For example 16 * 12 = 192. That means you can decrypt K3 if you cut it into a matrix of width 16 and rotate 90 degrees left, then cut into matrix of width 12 and rotate 90 degrees. Same for 48*4=192. Cut by 48, rotate left, cut by 4, rotate left will also decrypt K3.

Unfortunately, this only works when (336 mod A) + (336 mod B) = 0. That is to say the matrix needs to fit all 336 characters into a perfect rectangle. So decrypting with 3*64=192 doesn't work because 336 mod 64 = 16 which means the last row in the matrix will only fill up to 16 characters, and the rest of the row would be empty. You will see it only partially decrypts using 2*96, 3*64, and 6*32.

What is the magic number? 8.

I hope that helps.

-DS

t:
Based on what I've found, Anders, ROT's is a way to go for uncovering Sanborn's preset clues, and since a ridiculous number of them are found not just in the Morse, but in the K4 ciphertext, I'm guessing that they're a part of whatever "masking step" of cryptographic puzzles Sanborn employed. It goes a long way to explaining the "nuance of I QLUS", Tut and the Clock since.... the eyes on Tut's headdress are a clock based on a boat's passage through the hours. Nuance being night and day.

ROT is nice because it's easy pencil and paper work, the simplest of positive and negative Caesar shifts, and even easier if one substitutes an Excel spreadhseet.

A fine example here, and the answer to a riddle. What is the apex of a pyramid? A BENBEN. Or in ROT ->

What I also found also was that simply swapping the letter 'E' and 'K' in ITA-2 pretty much evens out the 1's and 0's as well. If you simply just did that and then transmitted a large English like corpus via ITA-2 is would be close to 52 zeros vs 48 ones. You'll still have as many 'E's (12.7%) but is is encoded with K's ITA-2 pattern of "01.111" and vice versa.

In fact, ignoring the whole binary encoding theory, it may simply be a direct hint just to swap those the 'E' and 'K' characters with each other. And, yeah, other transpositions do as much as well...

The trick with evening out the 1's and 0's to hide the English frequencies is that:
     1) you must have been transmitting English on the wire, it was highly skewed and you need to hide that skewness e.g. you just shuffled all of your letters like K3 and have a lot of Es and Ts to hide
     2) you started with English, enciphered it via some classical method & still end up with some skewed results (not necessarily English frequencies). So now you need to hide that skewness so as not to reveal your enciphering method/English peeking through

Anyway, K4 does appear 50:50. Determining the method that was used to get it from K4 plaintext (English skewed? How much?) back to 50:50 as a natural result of an enciphering method is the next step. Hi Larry,

Good food for thought, made me have another look at ITA-2 and did find an interesting property related to the K0 forward/reverse Morse examples.

* All of the ITA-2 binary representations of A-Z can have there bits reverse and still have a matching proper character e.g.
10111    11101    Q
11101    10111    X

* However, Just reversing all characters is equivalent to a classical 1:1 substitution, so nothing exciting there and you just get a new A-Z mapping ...

* Reversing every character's bit - when the sum of those bits is an odd number of 1's produces a new character e.g.

Even bits - stays the same --> 10111    10111    Q    --> Q
Odd bits - reverse the bits --> 10011    11001    W    --> B

* The remarkable property is that the new alphabet (with the odd summed bit characters reversed) is that there are no duplicated letters - you get a completely useable & reversible alphabetic substitution process based on it's odd/even "sentence" position...

Perhaps these alphabets were generated by Schiedt and then just the process was handed to Sanborn to use?

Cheers, Mike

I tend to think palindrome is what is being projected. Already mentioned is (I)NTERPRETA(TI..) and INVISIBL(E). There are less lengthy examples also.

Of course, SOS/VTB/EIOIE, etc. (EIEIO would not qualify!) is palindromic as a single Morse prosign. 111333111. It is also palindromic when run as a consecutive series. 1113331110111333111. When you reverse the Morse, you get the same thing.

On the other hand, RQ is not palindromic. 01010 11101. But, when you reverse the morse, you get YR. YR is palindromic and displays as a consecutive set of 1s and 0s. 10101 01010. When YR is run consecutively (YRYRYR)on a radioteletype machine it sounds like a continuous series of dits, 10101010101010, etc. Obviously, this is also palindromic.
When you see it this way, it becomes more evident that palindromes somehow enter the Kryptos picture.
PaulK

Hi Doug,

I happily get to play in this space (artificial intelligence/machine learning --> AI/ML) as my day job *occasionally*. I've also had a play with IBM quantum computers/simulators as per of learning new tech for work.

The challenge with these technologies (I'll exclude for Watson for the moment as it is more a expert knowledge representation/extraction engine and not my area of expertise) is the proper framing/encoding of the question. Then the limiting of the chosen parameters for failure/success and, with ML in particular, designing a fitness measure so that the algorithms can optimise against that score. Both gradient descent and hill climbing work against such a score and optimise along the way - that includes neural network like implementations as well.

I chose not to answer your question immediately as it did provide some food for thought that I wanted to chase down first that itself was lurking around in the back of my mind :)

How did Scheidt come up with something so diabolically uncrackable?!

In ML (& maths/stats included of course)  there is a multiple linear regression (MLR) technique that is used to fit a number of parameters to a single outcome/prediction e.g. Number of rooms in a house; Area of the land etc; car parking spots --> $$$ of the predicted house prices.

What people mostly don't learn mostly is that it (MLR) can be also represented as a huge list of functions/examples and those themselves can be written into a matrix form - multiply that matrix by the transposition of itself ( a single rotation of itself) , and Boom!, out comes the optimised formula (listed variable weights) to predict the house prices based on those examples encoded into the matrix.

So, how do you use matrices to create a diabolical uncrackable code?

Well, first we need move on to linear programming as opposed to the simpler matrix based fitting above - and here, we need to seek experts in this area...

You can also pen and paper it out with sufficient background knowledge of techniques/counter techniques I'd reckon - certainly Scheidt would and his close knit group be the most capable & certainly Scheidt as he did say it was "unique on the planet" or thereabouts....

However!

Loosely, we start with defining the goal K4function({'B','E','R','L','I','N'}) --> {'N','Y','P','V',T','T'} & it's symmetrical equivalent constraint K4function({'N','Y','P','V',T','T'}) --> {'B','E','R','L','I','N'}.

We also define that IOC({'N','Y','P','V',T','T'}) is really low. We can add the additional limitations to the linear programming model that bigrams({'N','Y','P','V',T','T'}) and trigrams({'N','Y','P','V',T','T'}) are likewise singular and non-existent over any series of CT rotations/regular manipluations.

And what else?

We could also allow the underlying 'B' and 'N' of those letters above to be encoded as any 5-bit binary notation that the linear programming model optimises/decides best fits the constraints e.g. 'A' --> 00001; 'B'--> '01000'...

The beauty of things like "linear programming" is it will optimise out an encoding method/solution that is potentially simple to remember/implement e.g. Chaocipher, but so rich in complexity that it is computationally too expensive to crack unless you've state based resourcing e.g. NSA, CIA et al.

More importantly, because we encoded the constraints as well (unlike MLR) , it will also have those feature/constraints built in. Further, if Sanborn used that same technique, then added extra treatments/encoding steps then those would probably not undo/reveal the original method ...

So, in  answer to your question: If no one has thrown Kryptos at Watson, then, firstly, we need to encode the problem to get to a stage where Watson (or linear programming) can run with it automatically...

The question for all of us is: What are our constraints/parameters to plug in?

Once we've those encoded then we hit [ENTER] :)

Kind regards, Mike
